title: Brackets, scaled orders & native SL invariant
body:
## Context
CandleViewer's single locked safety invariant is that **every position the product opens carries a native exchange-side stop-loss** (`docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` "Locked decisions"; `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 8.8; architecture principle **P4** in `docs/plan/20-architecture.md`; `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0008-trade-group-fanout.md`). `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` RSK-016 — "an order reaches the exchange without a native stop-loss" — is the highest-impact risk in the project, because an emulated stop dies with our backend process while a native stop lives inside Bybit's matching engine.

E32 is where that policy sentence becomes enforced code at a **single choke point** inside **M14 (OMS / execution)** and **M17 (risk, caps & kill-switch)**, together with the order-structure features that make the invariant liveable day to day: brackets as first-class objects, partial-fill-aware protective sizing, take-profit ladders, scaled/laddered entries, DCA safety ladders with a shared stop, break-even automation, and trailing stops translated from the product's percentage/ATR UX into Bybit's **price-distance** `trading-stop.trailingStop` field (`24-internal-schemas.md` section 8.9).

The epic sits in train **R3 Trading on demo** (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` section 7, sprints **S16-S17**) and is on the R3 critical path `E09 -> E27 -> E29 -> E32 -> E34 -> E43 -> E44` (section 11). Section 12 rule 2 is explicit: *"No order-placing UI ships before the key vault (E27), risk caps and kill-switch (E39), and the native-SL invariant (E32) are Done — this ordering is a safety requirement, not a preference."* R3 exit criterion #2 belongs to this epic: an automated suite must attempt, by **every** available path, to open a position without a native SL and observe **zero escapes**.

Research backing: Bybit v5 exposes attached TP/SL on `POST /v5/order/create` and a price-distance trailing stop on `POST /v5/position/trading-stop`, but exposes **no** OCO, iceberg, TWAP or scaled-order primitive; ladders therefore ride the batch-create endpoint (max 10 orders/request, `linear` supported, partial success possible) per `24-internal-schemas.md` section 10.6.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **User stories (domain ALGO — the bracket/ladder/stop subset; the emulated OCO/iceberg/TWAP/chase/monitor subset is E33):**
  - `US-ALGO-001` Bracket orders (**Must**) — E32-S01, E32-S05
  - `US-ALGO-003` Partial take-profit ladders (Should) — E32-S02, E32-S07
  - `US-ALGO-004` Scaled entry orders (Should) — E32-S03, E32-S06
  - `US-ALGO-008` Trailing stops, fixed and percentage (**Must**) — E32-S04, E32-S07
  - `US-ALGO-009` DCA / scale-in safety ladders (Should) — E32-S03, E32-S06
  - Cross-cutting: the native-SL invariant relied on by `US-ORD-007`..`US-ORD-010`, `US-POS-004` and R3 exit criterion #2.
- **Screens:** `SCR-069` Emulated OCO / bracket builder (**bracket half only**; the standalone-OCO half is E33), `SCR-065` Scaled / ladder order builder, `SCR-064` Position SL/TP editor (modal).
- **Components:** `CMP-119` BracketEditor, `CMP-120` TrailingStopEditor, `CMP-158` SafetyInvariantNotice, `CMP-228` PreviewTile, `CMP-118` AlgoProgressCard (`algoType="scaled"`); reused `CMP-001` Button, `CMP-010` Slider, `CMP-043` Dialog, `CMP-049` Table, `CMP-100` PriceInput, `CMP-101` QtyInput, `CMP-130` SlippageEstimateChip, `CMP-227` EstimatedBadge.
- **Backend modules:** **M14** OMS (`BracketSupervisor`, `ScaledSupervisor`, `TrailingTranslator`, native-SL attach path) and **M17** risk/caps (`NativeSlGuard`, `UnprotectedPositionWatchdog`).
- **API:** `POST /api/v1/orders`, `PATCH /api/v1/orders/{orderId}`, `DELETE /api/v1/orders/{orderId}`, `GET /api/v1/orders`, `GET /api/v1/orders/{orderId}/diagnostics`, `POST /api/v1/trade-groups`, `POST /api/v1/trade-groups/preview`, `POST /api/v1/trade-groups/{tradeGroupId}/amend`, `POST /api/v1/trade-groups/{tradeGroupId}/cancel`, `PUT /api/v1/positions/{positionId}/tpsl`; schemas `AlgoSpec` (`bracket`, `scaled`), `AlgoKind`, `TpSlMode`, `TrailingStopSpec`.
- **WS topics:** `orders`, `positions`, `executions`, `trade_groups`, `system` — including `TradeGroupLeg.native_sl_confirmed` / `native_sl_confirmed_at` reaching the wire.
- **DB tables:** `trade_groups` (`algo`, `algo_params`), `trade_group_legs` (`native_sl_confirmed`, `native_sl_confirmed_at`, partial index `ix_tgl_no_sl`), `orders` (`parent_order_id`, `intent`, `order_link_id`), `order_events`, `executions`, `positions`, `account_profiles` (`require_native_sl`, `fallback_sl_offset`), `audit_log`; enums `algo_kind`, `order_intent`.
- **ADR:** `27-adrs/ADR-0028-native-sl-invariant-and-brackets.md` (new, written in E32-T04).

## Out of scope
- Emulated **OCO**, **iceberg**, **TWAP**, **chase** and the **algo monitor panel** (`US-ALGO-002/005/006/007/010`, `SCR-066/067/068/070`) — epic **E33**.
- Multi-account **fan-out** orchestration, the rate-limit governor and partial-failure unwind — epic **E34** (E32 supplies the per-leg bracket/native-SL semantics E34 replicates).
- The order ticket itself (`SCR-060`..`SCR-062`) — epic **E30**; chart/DOM drag-to-amend — epic **E31**.
- Risk caps, lockouts and the kill-switch mechanics — epic **E39** (E32 consumes them).
- Rule-engine authored ATR/structure/MA trails evaluated per bar — epics **E35/E36/E37** (E32 provides only the tighten-only `trading-stop` write path they call).
- Live trading. Everything here executes against **Bybit demo**; the live gate is E44.
- Android; any non-Bybit exchange; spot/inverse/option instruments (USDT linear perps only).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The invariant holds across every entry path
  Given the zero-escape suite exercises the order ticket, chart drag, DOM click, rule action, fan-out leg, bracket, scaled ladder and DCA ladder
  When each path attempts to open a position without a native exchange-side stop-loss
  Then every attempt is rejected before any request reaches Bybit, an audit row is written, and the suite records zero escapes

Scenario: A bracket behaves as one object end to end
  Given a bracket with an entry, a native stop and a three-step take-profit ladder on Bybit demo
  When the entry partially fills and then fully fills
  Then protective quantities track the filled quantity at every step, the 30-second reconciliation job finds no orphaned protective orders, and cancelling the entry before any fill cancels every dependent protective order

Scenario: A percentage trailing stop reaches Bybit as a price distance
  Given a 1.5% trailing stop configured on a long position in SCR-064
  When the OMS arms it
  Then TrailingTranslator converts the percentage to an absolute quote-currency distance, writes it with both TP and SL sides in one POST /v5/position/trading-stop call, shows the distance and trigger price in the UI, and only ever tightens it thereafter

Scenario: Backend dies between entry fill and stop attach (failure)
  Given the process is killed after an entry fills and before the position-level stop is attached
  When the backend restarts
  Then the watchdog detects the unprotected position within 10 seconds, attaches the fallback stop at profile.fallback_sl_offset, raises a critical NakedPositionAlert, and the position is never left unprotected

Scenario: A ladder that cannot be split is refused, not silently rounded away
  Given a scaled or DCA ladder whose per-level quantity would fall below the instrument minimum lot
  When the user requests it
  Then sub-minimum levels are dropped and their quantity redistributed to the survivors, and if no viable ladder exists the request is refused with an explanation and a single-order alternative offered
```

## Technical notes / design
- **Choke point, not call sites.** Per RSK-016 mitigation the invariant is enforced in the one function through which *all* submission passes (`OMS.submit`), not sprinkled at each caller. E32-T01 builds that guard; E30/E31/E33/E34/E35 inherit it for free.
- **Attach, don't chase.** Section 8.8 rule 1: entries carry `stopLoss` on `POST /v5/order/create` so there is no window of exposure. Only when attachment is impossible (algo children that would over-attach) does the OMS place a position-level stop within a **2 s** deadline, backed by a **5 s** watchdog scan and a >10 s critical alert.
- **Only-tighten ratchet.** Section 8.8 rule 5: break-even, ATR/structure/MA trails and rule-engine stops may only tighten the native stop; loosening requires an explicit, audited user confirmation.
- **Bracket model** (`BracketParams`, section 10.7): native attached `stopLoss`, plus `takeProfit` when there is exactly one TP leg and `tpsl_mode="full"`; multi-leg TP ladders are reduce-only limit children placed on first fill and re-sized per section 9.3.3.
- **Scaled model** (`ScaledParams`, section 10.6): `levels` 2..50, equal/linear/geometric/custom distribution with `skew`, conservative rounding, duplicate-price merge, remainder to the level nearest `price_start`, sub-minimum levels dropped and redistributed, batch submission at 10 orders/request with per-item `retCode` handling.
- **Trailing translation lives in the OMS, never the UI** (`20-architecture.md` section 9 rule 6).
- **Protective reserve.** `RateBudget.reserved_for_protective` (section 8.7) guarantees a stop placement or flatten always gets a token even while a 50-level ladder saturates the entry bucket; protective traffic uses `priority="critical"`.

## Test plan
- **Unit** (>=90% on M14/M17 per the R3 local policy, absolute floor >=85%): invariant guard truth table; bracket child sizing under partial fills; TP-ladder rounding; scaled weight/rounding/merge/redistribute maths; trailing unit translation; only-tighten ratchet.
- **Contract:** OpenAPI + WS schema tests for `AlgoSpec.bracket`/`.scaled`, `PUT /positions/{positionId}/tpsl`, `TradeGroupLeg.native_sl_confirmed`.
- **Integration:** recorded Bybit demo fixtures — partial fills, rejections, `10018` rate-limit, batch partial success, WS disconnect mid-bracket, clock skew.
- **E2E:** Playwright web + Electron over SCR-069, SCR-065, SCR-064.
- **Perf:** budget #4 — submit->ack p95 <300 ms on demo end-to-end, backend-added <=50 ms p95.
- **Chaos:** process kill between entry fill and stop attach; Postgres failover mid-ladder; exchange 5xx during TP-ladder placement.
- **Safety suite (required merge check):** the zero-escape invariant suite (E32-Q01).

## Security notes
Per `04-security-program.md` and `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 8, everything touching `area/oms-execution` order placement or the fan-out safety invariant is **always** treated as `security`-labelled. Threats: tampering with a bracket payload to strip the stop; elevation via a rule or API client that bypasses the choke point; repudiation of a loosened stop without an audit row; denial of service by a 50-level ladder burning the account rate budget so a protective order cannot be placed. Controls: server-side-only enforcement, RBAC `orders:write` plus account scope on every path, audit rows for every stop modification (`position.stop_modified`, `position.tp_ladder_set`, `algo.scaled_created`), the protective rate reserve, and the ladder level cap. Data classification: financial/transactional.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA on SCR-064, SCR-065, SCR-069. The generated ladder is previewed as a real table (level, price, qty, cumulative qty, cumulative notional, resulting average); R-multiples and percentages are both shown as text; the native-SL guarantee is a persistent `role="note"` (CMP-158), never a tooltip or toast; every drag-equivalent has a keyboard path; "(estimated)" is in the accessible name wherever CMP-227 appears.

## Performance notes
Budget #4 (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` section 5.2): submit->ack p95 <300 ms on demo end-to-end, backend-added <=50 ms p95; fan-out adds <=10 ms/account. Native-SL attach must complete inside the same window or the "protective stop pending" state must be surfaced. The scaled-ladder preview recomputes locally within one frame (<=16.6 ms).

## Observability
Metrics `oms_native_sl_attach_seconds`, `oms_native_sl_missing_total`, `oms_invariant_reject_total{path}`, `oms_bracket_children_total{state}`, `oms_scaled_levels_submitted_total{result}`, `oms_trailing_updates_total{kind}`, plus the existing `order_submit_seconds{transport,env}`. Critical alert `NakedPositionAlert`. Audit events `algo.scaled_created`, `algo.scaled_cancelled`, `algo.scaled_partially_cancelled`, `position.stop_modified`, `position.tp_ladder_set`. Structured logs carry `trade_group_id`, `algo_id`, `order_link_id`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every child Story/Task/Spike/Design/QA/Security ticket Done or explicitly descoped with a recorded disposition.
- [ ] R3 exit criterion #2 demonstrated: zero escapes from the invariant suite across all entry paths, suite wired as a **required merge check**.
- [ ] Coverage >=90% on M14/M17, >=85% backend overall, >=80% frontend.
- [ ] `24-internal-schemas.md` sections 8.8/10.6/10.7, `22-api-openapi.yaml`, `23-ws-protocol.md` reflect shipped behaviour; ADR-0016 merged.
- [ ] a11y: axe-core green on SCR-064/065/069 plus one manual screen-reader pass each.
- [ ] perf: budget #4 numbers recorded on demo.
- [ ] security: STRIDE finalised, Critical/High closed, Security-engineer sign-off comment.
- [ ] QA: epic-level regression plus exploratory pass recorded and signed off.
- [ ] Design: CDO sign-off on SCR-064/065/069 and the design-QA sweep closed.
- [ ] Demoed to Owner at a Sprint Review against **staging (demo)**; Owner acceptance recorded.

## Dependencies
- **E29 OMS core & order state machine** — supplies `OMS.submit`, the order state machine, `orderLinkId` idempotency and the reconciliation loop the guard hooks into (roadmap graph `E29 --> E32`).
- **E39 Risk caps, lockouts & kill-switch** — the M17 module the guard lives beside; ladders must respect caps and halt on kill-switch (`E39 --> E32`).
- **E28 Per-account profiles & trade groups** — `profile.require_native_sl`, `profile.fallback_sl_offset`, sizing rules and SL/TP offsets.
- **E27 Accounts & API-key vault** — demo credentials for integration tests.
- **E30 Order ticket UI** — hosts the three modals and supplies `CMP-107 OrderTicket`, the arm/lock control and the environment badge the FE stories compose with.
- Downstream: **E33** (emulated algos build on bracket/native-SL semantics), **E34** (fan-out replicates them per leg).

## Branch

title: Measure attached-SL versus trading-stop attach latency and failure modes on demo
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 8.8 allows two ways a position acquires its native stop: **attached** on `POST /v5/order/create` (`stopLoss` field, rule 1) or **position-level** via `POST /v5/position/trading-stop` on first fill within a 2 s deadline (rule 2). The whole E32 design — the choke point (E32-T01), the watchdog deadline (E32-T02) and the bracket child-sizing policy (E32-S01) — depends on numbers we do not have yet: how long each path actually takes on Bybit demo, which Bybit `retCode`s each path returns when it fails, and whether attached SL survives partial fills and amends. Guessing these would mean re-deriving them under deadline pressure in S16, on the R3 critical path.

Section 8.9 also records a known trap: one-sided TP/SL modification via `trading-stop` breaks Bybit's OCO pairing, so our writes must always send both sides. The spike must confirm this on demo rather than trusting the note.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Timeboxed **3 days**, `spike/e32-sl-attach-latency`, throwaway harness (not production code).
- Harness in `services/oms/spikes/sl_attach_bench.py` driving a Bybit **demo** account from E27's vault against `api-demo.bybit.com`, USDT linear perps only (`BTCUSDT`, `ETHUSDT`, plus one low-liquidity symbol).
- Measure, >=200 samples per arm: (a) `order/create` with attached `stopLoss` -> ack latency; (b) `order/create` without SL, then `position/trading-stop` on first execution event -> confirmed latency, measured from the WS execution timestamp.
- Record failure taxonomy: every distinct `retCode`/`retMsg` returned by each arm, mapped to the internal taxonomy in section 8.6.
- Answer explicitly: does attached `stopLoss` survive (1) a partial fill, (2) a `PATCH` amend of the entry price, (3) a reduce-only child placed against the same position, (4) hedge-mode `positionIdx=1/2`?
- Confirm the one-sided-write OCO-pairing trap and the correct both-sides write shape.
- Measure the rate-limit cost of each arm (requests per protected position) to feed `RateBudget.reserved_for_protective` sizing in section 8.7.

## Out of scope
- Any production code; live environment; non-Bybit venues; batch/ladder submission (covered by E32-S03's own measurements).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Both arms are measured with a decision-grade sample
  Given the harness has run at least 200 samples per arm on Bybit demo across three symbols
  When results are tabulated
  Then p50/p95/p99 latency, success rate and the full retCode histogram are reported per arm, and the report states whether the 2 s attach deadline in section 8.8 rule 2 is achievable with margin

Scenario: The attached-SL survival questions are answered
  Given partial fill, entry amend, reduce-only child and hedge-mode scenarios are each executed at least 10 times
  Then the report states for each, with evidence, whether the attached stopLoss persists, is cleared, or is silently altered

Scenario: The trading-stop pairing trap is confirmed or refuted (edge)
  Given a position with both TP and SL set
  When only the SL side is written via trading-stop
  Then the observed effect on the TP side is recorded, and the report prescribes the exact request shape E32-T01 must use

Scenario: The spike ends in a decision, not a document (failure path)
  Given the measurements show the 2 s deadline is not achievable on demo
  Then the ADR records "attach-only, refuse orders that cannot carry an attached SL" as the chosen fallback, and follow-up tickets are filed against E32-T01 and E32-T02 before the spike closes
```

## Technical notes / design
- Drive the harness through E29's adapter so measurements reflect real client overhead, not a bespoke HTTP client.
- Latency for arm (b) is measured from the `execution` WS message's exchange timestamp to the `trading-stop` HTTP 200, which is the interval the 2 s deadline actually covers.
- Clock skew: record `X-Bapi-*` response headers and the exchange timestamp with every sample; discard samples where local-vs-exchange skew exceeds 500 ms.
- Emit raw samples to a Parquet file under `artifacts/spikes/e32-k01/` so the numbers can be re-analysed rather than only summarised.
- Decision criteria agreed with the Architect up front: if arm (b) p99 > 1.5 s, the OMS defaults to attach-only and algo children that would over-attach are restructured rather than accepting a trading-stop window.

## Test plan
No production tests. The harness self-checks that each sample has a matching execution event and a matching position state, discarding incomplete samples; the discard rate is reported.

## Security notes
Uses a **demo** key only, read from the E27 vault at runtime — never inlined, never committed. Raw artifacts must not contain the API key, account UID, or IP; the harness redacts these on write. No live credentials may be configured for this ticket (enforced by the environment gate in M1).

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI.

## Performance notes
This ticket *produces* the performance inputs for budget #4 (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` section 5.2); it is not itself gated by a budget.

## Observability
The harness emits the same metric names the production path will use (`oms_native_sl_attach_seconds`) so the dashboards built in E32-T02 can be validated against spike data before real traffic exists.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Both arms measured, tables and histograms published in the ticket.
- [ ] All four attached-SL survival questions answered with evidence.
- [ ] ADR-0016 draft section "attach vs trading-stop" written (merged later by E32-T04).
- [ ] Follow-up tickets filed or explicitly not needed, with reason.
- [ ] `32-risk-register.md` RSK-016 updated with the measured residual-exposure window.
- [ ] Findings presented at Sprint Review; branch archived unmerged.

## Dependencies
`E27` (demo key vault), `E29` (adapter + order state machine to measure through).

## Branch

title: Enforce the native-SL invariant at the single OMS submission choke point
body:
> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** this ticket's lifecycle is now built directly on `xstate-statemachine` 0.9.1 via `statechart.factory` from the first line of code (catalogue B8). No in-house shim, no dual-runtime harness, no hand-rolled state enum/transition table. The protection region becomes a chart with the B610-OC-CD03 attempt counter; the choke-point guard stays.

## Context
This is the ticket that makes RSK-016 ("an order reaches the exchange without a native stop-loss", `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md`) structurally impossible rather than merely discouraged. `24-internal-schemas.md` section 8.8 states the invariant; `21-database-schema.md` enforces the intent at rest (`account_profiles.require_native_sl` with `CONSTRAINT ap_native_sl CHECK (require_native_sl = true)`); this ticket enforces it in flight.

The design decision — taken in E32-X01's threat model and recorded here — is that the guard lives at **one** function, `OMS.submit()` in M14, through which every submission path already passes (order ticket E30, chart/DOM E31, brackets and ladders E32, emulated algos E33, fan-out legs E34, rule actions E35). Enforcement at call sites was rejected: every new caller would be a new escape hatch, and R3 exit criterion #2 demands zero escapes across paths that do not all exist yet.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `services/oms/risk/native_sl_guard.py` — `NativeSlGuard` (module **M17**), a pure, synchronous pre-flight evaluated inside `OMS.submit()` before any adapter call.
- Classification helper `is_position_opening(intent, reduce_only, position_state)` — `intent in {entry, scale_in, reverse}` or any non-`reduce_only` order that would increase absolute position size in the target `positionIdx`.
- Three outcomes: **PASS_ATTACHED** (request carries `stopLoss`), **PASS_DEFERRED** (attachment impossible; a `trading-stop` write is scheduled with a 2 s deadline and a `pending_native_sl` row is written transactionally *before* the adapter call), **REJECT** (no stop and no viable deferral) with error code `NATIVE_SL_REQUIRED`.
- Deferral is only permitted for reasons enumerated in a closed allow-list (`algo_child_over_attach`, `batch_ladder_leg`); any other reason rejects. The allow-list is a constant, not configuration.
- `orders.intent`, `trade_group_legs.native_sl_confirmed` / `native_sl_confirmed_at` writes; audit rows on every REJECT and every deferral.
- Wire `oms_invariant_reject_total{path,reason}` and `oms_native_sl_attach_seconds` metrics.
- Kill-switch and risk-cap consultation: the guard calls E39's `RiskGate` first, so a halted system rejects before the invariant question is even asked.
- Feature flag: **none**. The guard is unconditional; there is deliberately no flag that can disable it (recorded as a decision in the body of ADR-0016).
- Implement the `B8` lifecycle as `statechart/machines/B08.position_protection.machine.json` (committed by E50-S01/S02, hash-locked). Do not hand-write the state enum or transition table.
- Build it only through `statechart.factory.build('position_protection', lane=...)`, and restore it only through `statechart.persistence.restore`.
- Write guards, actions and services in `statechart/bindings/08_position_protection.py` as a `MachineLogic`. Everything is `async def`, and services are idempotent under re-entry.
- Add `tests/xstate_contract/test_08_position_protection.py`, which becomes a member of the blocking gate.
- All sends go through `statechart.gateway`.

## Out of scope
- The watchdog / fallback attach (E32-T02), bracket structure (E32-S01), ladders (E32-S03), trailing translation (E32-S04), any UI.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A position-opening order without a stop is rejected before the adapter
  Given a market buy with intent "entry", reduce_only false and no stopLoss
  When OMS.submit is called
  Then the guard returns REJECT with error code NATIVE_SL_REQUIRED, no request reaches the exchange adapter (asserted by a strict adapter mock that fails the test if called), an audit row is written, and oms_invariant_reject_total{path,reason} increments

Scenario: A reduce-only closing order is allowed without a stop
  Given a reduce-only sell against an existing long
  When OMS.submit is called
  Then the guard classifies it as non-position-opening and passes it through unchanged

Scenario: A deferred attach is persisted before the order is sent
  Given an algo child that cannot carry an attached stopLoss and whose reason is on the allow-list
  When OMS.submit is called
  Then a pending_native_sl row with a 2 s deadline is committed before the adapter call, and if the process dies immediately after the adapter call the restarted process finds that row

Scenario: An unknown deferral reason is rejected, not tolerated (edge)
  Given a caller requests deferral with a reason not on the closed allow-list
  Then the guard returns REJECT, logs at error level with the offending reason, and the caller receives NATIVE_SL_REQUIRED

Scenario: The kill-switch pre-empts the invariant check (failure)
  Given the E39 kill-switch is active
  When any position-opening submission is attempted
  Then RiskGate rejects first with KILL_SWITCH_ACTIVE, and the invariant counter is not incremented (so kill-switch activity does not pollute invariant telemetry)

Scenario: Hedge mode is handled per positionIdx (edge)
  Given hedge mode with an existing long on positionIdx 1
  When a buy on positionIdx 1 without a stop is submitted
  Then it is rejected as position-opening; a sell reduce-only on positionIdx 1 passes
```

## Technical notes / design
- Signature: `NativeSlGuard.evaluate(req: PlaceOrderRequest, pos: PositionState | None, profile: AccountProfile) -> GuardVerdict`. Pure function of its inputs; no I/O, so it is exhaustively unit-testable as a truth table.
- `GuardVerdict = Literal["pass_attached","pass_deferred","reject"]` plus `reason: str` and `deadline_ms: int | None`.
- Placement: inside `OMS.submit()`, after idempotency-key resolution and after `RiskGate`, before `adapter.place_order()`. An architecture test asserts `adapter.place_order` has exactly one call site in the codebase (`tests/architecture/test_single_submit_path.py`) — this is what makes "choke point" mechanically true and is a required check.
- Deferral persistence uses the same transaction as the `order_events` write-ahead row from E29, so the sequence is: persist intent -> persist pending attach -> send. Never send first.
- `profile.require_native_sl` is read but cannot be false (DB CHECK); the code still asserts it and raises a configuration error if it is, guarding against a future migration loosening the constraint.
- Error code `NATIVE_SL_REQUIRED` maps to HTTP 422 in `22-api-openapi.yaml` and to a user-facing message defined in E32-D07's handoff pack.
Normative contract: `28-statechart-catalogue.md` §B8.1-.8. Mandatory config: 29-statechart-adoption-plan §1.2 (79-r14 §7 FINAL block). Hot-path parts listed in 29 §3 stay plain code.

## Test plan
- **Unit (target >=95% on this module):** full truth table across intent x reduce_only x position_state x stopLoss present x position mode x deferral reason; hedge/one-way; zero-qty and rounding edges.
- **Architecture test:** single call site of `adapter.place_order` — fails the build otherwise.
- **Integration:** against recorded Bybit demo fixtures, confirm attached-SL orders round-trip and deferred ones create the pending row.
- **Contract:** `NATIVE_SL_REQUIRED` appears in the OpenAPI error enum and the WS `orders` rejection payload.
- **Property test:** for randomly generated submissions, assert the invariant "if the adapter was called with a position-opening request then either stopLoss was present or a pending row exists".
- Coverage gate >=90% for M14/M17.
- Pure-API unit tests of the binding module with a `SimulatedClock`.
- Contract-suite membership, covering both spellings and every §B8.7 invariant.
- A snapshot round-trip (persist->restore) at every quiescence point the ticket introduces, plus a refused restore on a hash or HMAC mismatch.

## Security notes
STRIDE (E32-X01): **Tampering** — a client stripping `stopLoss` from the payload is defeated because the guard is server-side and the profile flag cannot be disabled. **Elevation** — a rule-engine action or internal caller attempting to bypass is defeated by the single-call-site architecture test. **Repudiation** — every REJECT and deferral writes an `audit_log` row with actor, account, symbol and reason. **DoS** — the guard is pure and O(1); it cannot be made slow by input. Data classification: financial/transactional. Requires Security-engineer review before merge (label `security`).

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend only. The user-facing rejection copy is specified in E32-D07 and consumed by E30/E32 UI stories.

## Performance notes
The guard must add <=1 ms p99 to `OMS.submit`, inside budget #4's <=50 ms backend-added allowance (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` section 5.2). Asserted by a micro-benchmark in CI.

## Observability
`oms_invariant_reject_total{path,reason}`, `oms_native_sl_attach_seconds{mode=attached|deferred}`, `oms_native_sl_deferred_pending` gauge. Audit events `oms.native_sl_rejected`, `oms.native_sl_deferred`. Structured logs carry `order_link_id`, `trade_group_id`, `account_id`, `reason`.

## Definition of Done

title: Build the unprotected-position watchdog with fallback attach and alert
body:
> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** this ticket's lifecycle is now built directly on `xstate-statemachine` 0.9.1 via `statechart.factory` from the first line of code (catalogue B8). No in-house shim, no dual-runtime harness, no hand-rolled state enum/transition table. The watchdog is a chart state plus a coarse `after:`.

## Context
E32-T01 prevents unprotected orders from being *sent*. It cannot prevent a position becoming unprotected *afterwards*: a deferred attach can fail, the process can die between fill and attach, a user can cancel a stop directly on the Bybit app, or the exchange can drop a conditional order. `24-internal-schemas.md` section 8.8 rule 3 mandates the second line of defence — a watchdog scanning every open position every 5 s, raising a `critical` alert and auto-attaching a fallback stop for any position unprotected for >10 s. `21-database-schema.md` provisions the query: partial index `ix_tgl_no_sl ON trade_group_legs (trade_group_id) WHERE status IN ('open','partially_filled') AND native_sl_confirmed = false`, budgeted at <2 ms in the schema's access-pattern table (row 10, "safety monitor").

## Scope / Deliverables
- `services/oms/risk/sl_watchdog.py` — `UnprotectedPositionWatchdog` (module **M17**), an asyncio task started with the OMS.
- 5 s scan over open positions joined to `trade_group_legs` via `ix_tgl_no_sl`, plus a cross-check against the reconciler's exchange-truth snapshot from E29 so a position unknown to our DB is still caught.
- Deferred-attach deadline enforcement: `pending_native_sl` rows past their 2 s deadline are retried immediately (up to 3 attempts with 250 ms backoff) using `priority="critical"` so they draw on `RateBudget.reserved_for_protective` (section 8.7).
- Fallback attach at `profile.fallback_sl_offset` (default: the tighter of 2% and 3x ATR(14)) via `POST /v5/position/trading-stop`, writing **both** TP and SL sides in one call per the section 8.9 pairing caveat.
- `NakedPositionAlert` (severity `critical`) emitted on the `system` WS topic and through E40's delivery once available; degrades to log + metric if E40 is not yet deployed.
- Sets `native_sl_confirmed` / `native_sl_confirmed_at` on success; audit event `oms.native_sl_fallback_attached`.
- Escalation: if three fallback attempts fail, the watchdog raises `NakedPositionAlert` at `critical` **and** requests E39's account-level lockout for new entries on that account (never an automatic flatten — flattening is a documented manual runbook).
- Implement the `B8` lifecycle as `statechart/machines/B08.position_protection.machine.json` (committed by E50-S01/S02, hash-locked). Do not hand-write the state enum or transition table.
- Build it only through `statechart.factory.build('position_protection', lane=...)`, and restore it only through `statechart.persistence.restore`.
- Write guards, actions and services in `statechart/bindings/08_position_protection.py` as a `MachineLogic`. Everything is `async def`, and services are idempotent under re-entry.
- Add `tests/xstate_contract/test_08_position_protection.py`, which becomes a member of the blocking gate.
- All sends go through `statechart.gateway`.

## Out of scope
- Auto-flattening positions (explicitly forbidden — the kill-switch semantics in E39 are "stops new risk, does not force-close").
- The alert delivery channels themselves (E40); the risk lockout mechanism itself (E39).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A position that loses its stop is re-protected
  Given an open position whose native stop is cancelled out of band
  When the next 5-second scan runs
  Then within 10 seconds of the stop disappearing a fallback stop at profile.fallback_sl_offset is attached, native_sl_confirmed is set true, an audit row is written and a critical NakedPositionAlert is raised

Scenario: A missed deferred attach is retried before the watchdog interval
  Given a pending_native_sl row whose 2-second deadline has passed
  When the watchdog next runs
  Then the attach is retried immediately with priority critical drawing on the protective reserve, and succeeds or escalates within three attempts

Scenario: Repeated failure escalates rather than loops (failure)
  Given three consecutive fallback attach attempts fail with exchange 5xx
  Then the watchdog stops retrying, raises a critical alert naming the account, symbol and exposure, requests an E39 new-entry lockout for that account, and never attempts to flatten the position automatically

Scenario: A position unknown to our database is still caught (edge)
  Given the exchange reports an open position that has no matching trade_group_leg row
  When the scan cross-checks the reconciler snapshot
  Then the position is treated as unprotected until proven otherwise, adopted into the DB, and protected

Scenario: The scan stays within its query budget (edge)
  Given 500 open legs across 5 accounts
  When the scan runs
  Then the ix_tgl_no_sl query executes in under 2 ms as specified in 21-database-schema.md and the scan completes within one 5-second interval with margin
```

## Technical notes / design
- Config keys: `OmsConfig.native_sl_deadline_ms = 2000`, `native_sl_watchdog_interval_s = 5`, `native_sl_alert_after_s = 10`, `native_sl_fallback_max_attempts = 3` (`24-internal-schemas.md` section 16 configuration).
- The scan is idempotent and single-flight per account: a mutex per `exchange_account_id` prevents two overlapping scans double-attaching after a slow exchange response.
- Fallback offset is computed from the *entry/avg* price, not the current mark, so a fast adverse move cannot produce a stop on the wrong side; if the computed stop would already be through the mark, the watchdog attaches at the nearest permitted tick and flags the alert as `already_through_mark`.
- ATR(14) is read from the bar-builder cache (M7); if unavailable, the 2% branch is used and the degradation is logged — the watchdog must never block on market data.
- Ordering guarantee: the watchdog never runs on an account while an unwind plan (E34) is `running`, to avoid fighting the unwinder.
Normative contract: `28-statechart-catalogue.md` §B8.1-.8. Mandatory config: 29-statechart-adoption-plan §1.2 (79-r14 §7 FINAL block). Hot-path parts listed in 29 §3 stay plain code.

## Test plan
- **Unit:** offset computation (both branches, already-through-mark), retry/backoff, escalation after 3 failures, single-flight mutex, ATR-unavailable degradation.
- **Integration:** recorded fixtures for out-of-band stop cancellation, exchange 5xx on trading-stop, unknown-position adoption.
- **Chaos (E32-Q05 hosts the scenarios, this ticket provides hooks):** kill the process between fill and attach; assert re-protection within 10 s of restart.
- **Perf:** benchmark the scan at 500 open legs asserting <2 ms query time and <5 s total scan.
- Coverage >=90% on M17.
- Pure-API unit tests of the binding module with a `SimulatedClock`.
- Contract-suite membership, covering both spellings and every §B8.7 invariant.
- A snapshot round-trip (persist->restore) at every quiescence point the ticket introduces, plus a refused restore on a hash or HMAC mismatch.

## Security notes
STRIDE: **Denial of service** — a flood of unprotected positions could exhaust the rate budget; mitigated by the protective reserve and by per-account single-flight. **Repudiation** — every fallback attach and every escalation writes an audit row. **Information disclosure** — alerts name account IDs and sizes, so `NakedPositionAlert` payloads are RBAC-filtered on the `system` topic per `23-ws-protocol.md`. Security-engineer review required.

## Accessibility notes
N/A backend; the alert's UI presentation is covered by E40 and by CMP-158 usage in E32-S05/S06/S07.

## Performance notes
Scan query <2 ms (`21-database-schema.md` access-pattern row 10); full scan cycle well inside the 5 s interval at the R3 capacity target of 5 accounts x 10 symbols. Fallback attach latency counted against budget #4's protective window.

## Observability
Metrics `oms_native_sl_missing_total{account}`, `oms_native_sl_fallback_total{result}`, `oms_sl_watchdog_scan_seconds`, gauge `oms_positions_unprotected`. Alert rule `NakedPositionAlert` (critical, page). Audit `oms.native_sl_fallback_attached`, `oms.native_sl_escalated`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All acceptance scenarios covered by automated tests.
- [ ] Coverage >=90% on M17.

- [ ] Security-engineer review comment present.

title: Implement break-even automation as an only-tighten system behaviour
body:
## Context
`24-internal-schemas.md` section 10.7 `BracketParams` carries `move_to_breakeven_at_r` and `breakeven_offset_ticks` (default 2, to cover fees), and states that break-even and trailing are handled as system behaviours that **may only tighten** the native stop (section 8.8 rule 5). SCR-064's wireframe shows "Break-even at [1.0]R offset [+ fees]" as a first-class control. This ticket implements the backend behaviour so SCR-064 (E32-S07) has something to switch on, and so the rule engine (E35) inherits a tested ratchet rather than building its own.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `services/oms/algos/breakeven.py` — `BreakEvenSupervisor` (module M14), subscribing to position updates.
- Trigger: unrealised R-multiple >= `move_to_breakeven_at_r`, computed as `(mark - avg_entry) / (avg_entry - initial_stop)` signed by side, using the **initial** stop distance recorded at bracket creation so later tightening does not move the R denominator.
- Action: write a new stop at `avg_entry +/- breakeven_offset_ticks` via the shared tighten-only `trading-stop` write path from E32-S04 (both sides in one call).
- Ratchet enforcement: the write is refused if it would loosen the stop; refusal is logged and counted, not raised to the user as an error.
- Idempotency: fires at most once per position per arming; re-arms only if the position is closed and reopened, or the user explicitly resets it.
- `positions` WS topic surfaces `breakeven_armed` / `breakeven_applied_at` so the UI can render the state.
- Audit event `position.stop_modified` with `reason="breakeven"`.

## Out of scope
- ATR/structure/MA trails (E35 rule engine), the SCR-064 control itself (E32-S07), the trailing translation path (E32-S04, consumed here).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Break-even fires once at the configured R
  Given a long with avg entry 63,000, initial stop 62,800 and break-even at 1.0R with a 2-tick offset
  When the mark reaches 63,200
  Then the native stop is moved to 63,000 plus 2 ticks in one trading-stop call carrying both TP and SL, an audit row with reason "breakeven" is written, and the position reports breakeven_applied_at

Scenario: The R denominator is frozen at creation
  Given the stop has already been tightened by a trailing update
  When the break-even R is evaluated
  Then it still uses the initial stop distance recorded at bracket creation, so tightening the stop cannot retroactively make 1R easier to reach

Scenario: A loosening break-even write is refused (failure)
  Given the stop has already been trailed above the break-even price
  When the break-even trigger fires
  Then the write is refused as a would-loosen violation, a counter increments, the stop is unchanged, and no user-facing error is raised

Scenario: The trigger does not re-fire after a flicker (edge)
  Given the mark crosses 1R, break-even applies, and the mark falls back below 1R and crosses again
  Then break-even does not fire a second time for the same arming and no additional rate budget is consumed

Scenario: Position closed mid-evaluation (edge)
  Given the position is flattened between the trigger evaluation and the trading-stop write
  Then the write is abandoned on the "position is zero" exchange response, the algo ends cleanly, and no orphaned stop remains
```

## Technical notes / design
- Evaluation is driven by `positions` updates coalesced at 100 ms (`23-ws-protocol.md`), not by a timer, so the reaction is as fast as the feed without polling.
- `initial_stop` is persisted on the bracket row at creation (E32-S01) precisely so this computation is stable across restarts.
- All writes route through `TrailingTranslator.write_stop()` from E32-S04, which owns the both-sides rule, the ratchet and the rate-priority tagging — this ticket adds no second write path.
- Fee-aware offset: `breakeven_offset_ticks` defaults to 2 but the UI may express it as "+ fees"; the conversion from a fee estimate to ticks happens server-side using the instrument's taker fee and `tickSize`.

## Test plan
- **Unit:** R computation for long/short, frozen denominator, ratchet refusal, single-fire idempotency, fee-to-ticks conversion, flicker suppression.
- **Integration:** recorded fixture where the stop is already tighter; recorded fixture where the position closes mid-write.
- **E2E:** covered by E32-Q04 through SCR-064.
- Coverage >=90% on M14.

## Security notes
The ratchet is a safety control: a bug that loosens a stop is a P0 safety defect, not a functional one. Audit rows are mandatory for every stop movement (`position.stop_modified`). No new external surface is introduced.

## Accessibility notes
N/A backend; the SCR-064 presentation of break-even state is E32-S07.

## Performance notes
Evaluation must add <=0.5 ms per position update; the write inherits budget #4's amend path.

## Observability
Metrics `oms_breakeven_applied_total`, `oms_stop_loosening_refused_total{reason}`. Audit `position.stop_modified{reason=breakeven}`.

title: Make a bracket a first-class object with partial-fill-aware child sizing
body:
> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** this ticket's lifecycle is now built directly on `xstate-statemachine` 0.9.1 via `statechart.factory` from the first line of code (catalogue B8/B1). No in-house shim, no dual-runtime harness, no hand-rolled state enum/transition table. The bracket child lifecycle rides B1 and B8 charts; partial-fill sizing stays.

## Context
`US-ALGO-001` (**Must**) requires that entry, stop and target are submitted and tracked as **one** bracket: cancelling the entry cancels dependants leaving no orphans, and a partial fill makes protective quantities track the **filled** quantity rather than the requested one. Its NFR is absolute: *"no orphaned protective orders may ever remain — verified by a reconciliation job every 30 s."* `24-internal-schemas.md` section 10.7 (`BracketParams`) specifies "prefer native": the entry carries attached `stopLoss`, plus `takeProfit` when there is exactly one TP leg and `tpsl_mode="full"`; multi-leg ladders become reduce-only children sized per section 9.3.3.

Without this story the invariant guard from E32-T01 has nothing structured to guard: every downstream epic (E30 ticket, E31 chart/DOM, E33 algos, E34 fan-out) submits brackets, so the bracket object is the shared vocabulary.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Stories: `US-ALGO-001`.
- `services/oms/algos/bracket.py` — `BracketSupervisor` (module M14) implementing `AlgoSpec{kind="bracket"}` / `BracketParams` from section 10.7.
- Persistence: a `trade_groups` row with `algo='bracket'` and `algo_params`; `trade_group_legs` row carrying `native_sl_confirmed`; child `orders` rows linked by `parent_order_id` with `intent` in `{entry, stop_loss, take_profit}`; `initial_stop` recorded at creation for E32-T03's frozen R denominator.
- Submission: entry with attached `stopLoss` (and `takeProfit` for the single-leg full case) through `OMS.submit`, so E32-T01's guard returns PASS_ATTACHED.
- Partial-fill tracking: on each `executions` event, recompute protective quantity as the cumulative filled quantity, rounded to `qty_step`, and amend rather than cancel/replace where the exchange allows it.
- Cancellation cascade: cancelling an unfilled entry cancels every dependent protective order; cancelling a partially filled entry leaves the filled portion protected.
- Orphan reconciliation every 30 s: any protective order whose parent bracket has no corresponding position is cancelled and audited.
- API: `POST /api/v1/orders` with `algo.bracket`, `PATCH /api/v1/orders/{orderId}`, `DELETE /api/v1/orders/{orderId}`, `GET /api/v1/orders`; WS `orders`, `executions`, `positions`, `trade_groups`.
- Implement the `B8/B1` lifecycle as `statechart/machines/B08.position_protection.machine.json` (committed by E50-S01/S02, hash-locked). Do not hand-write the state enum or transition table.
- Build it only through `statechart.factory.build('position_protection', lane=...)`, and restore it only through `statechart.persistence.restore`.
- Write guards, actions and services in `statechart/bindings/08_position_protection.py` as a `MachineLogic`. Everything is `async def`, and services are idempotent under re-entry.
- Add `tests/xstate_contract/test_08_position_protection.py`, which becomes a member of the blocking gate.
- All sends go through `statechart.gateway`.

## Out of scope
- Multi-leg TP ladders (E32-S02), scaled entries (E32-S03), trailing (E32-S04), break-even (E32-T03), the SCR-069 UI (E32-S05), emulated OCO (E33), fan-out across accounts (E34).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A bracket is created as one object
  Given I submit an entry with a take-profit and a stop-loss for BTCUSDT on a demo account
  When the request is accepted
  Then one trade_groups row with algo 'bracket' and its child orders exist, the entry is sent to Bybit with attached stopLoss, and the orders panel and chart show a single bracket group rather than three unrelated orders

Scenario: Cancelling an unfilled entry leaves no orphans
  Given a bracket whose entry has not filled
  When I cancel the entry
  Then every dependent protective order is cancelled within the same operation, the 30-second reconciliation job finds no orphaned protective orders, and the bracket group closes with reason "entry cancelled"

Scenario: Protective quantity tracks a partial fill
  Given a bracket entry for 1.0 BTC that fills 0.4 BTC
  Then the protective stop quantity is amended to 0.4 BTC, the bracket detail shows filled 0.4 of 1.0, and when the remaining 0.6 fills the protective quantity becomes 1.0

Scenario: An amend of the protective order is rejected (error)
  Given a protective amend is rejected by Bybit because the order is already triggered
  Then the supervisor reconciles from executions rather than from intent, leaves the position protected by whatever native stop exists, raises a warning, and does not place a duplicate protective order

Scenario: Rounding makes the protective quantity unsendable (edge)
  Given a partial fill whose quantity rounds below the instrument minimum order quantity
  Then the protective order is left at the minimum sendable quantity covering the filled amount rather than being cancelled, so the position is never left without protection

Scenario: The process restarts mid-bracket (edge)
  Given the backend restarts after a partial fill but before the protective amend
  When it comes back
  Then the bracket state is rebuilt from Postgres and the exchange, the protective quantity is recomputed from executions, and the amend is sent once using the original idempotency key
```

## Technical notes / design
- Child `order_link_id`s follow E29's scheme with the group segment plus an incrementing `seq2` and an `ac` suffix (section 10.1 universal rule 4), making orphan adoption deterministic after a restart.
- Protective sizing rule: `protective_qty = floor_to_step(cumulative_filled_qty)`; if that is below `min_order_qty` but the filled quantity is non-zero, use `min_order_qty` and record the over-protection in the bracket detail (over-protecting is safe with `reduceOnly`; under-protecting is not).
- Prefer `amend` over cancel/replace throughout: one request instead of two, and no window with no protective order in the book.

title: Ship partial take-profit ladders that resize the stop as legs fill
body:
## Context
`US-ALGO-003` (Should) asks for staged take-profits: "25% at 1R, 25% at 2R and 50% at 3R" becomes three reduce-only orders with quantities rounded to lot size and the remainder assigned to the last leg; when the 1R leg fills the stop quantity adjusts to the remaining position automatically; and when the position is too small to split, the ladder is refused with an explanation and a single-target alternative offered. Its NFR requires ladder state persisted server-side and reconciled after restart.

This is the feature that makes SCR-064's "Take-profit ladder: 25% @ 1R / 25% @ 2R / 50% @ 3R" wireframe real, and it is the reason `tpsl_mode` exists as `partial` in section 8.9 — a multi-leg ladder cannot use Bybit's `Full` mode.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Stories: `US-ALGO-003`.
- Extends `BracketSupervisor` from E32-S01 with `take_profits: tuple[TakeProfitLeg, ...]` handling (section 10.7).
- Leg specification by percentage of position or absolute quantity, with price expressed as absolute price **or** R-multiple, resolved server-side against the bracket's `initial_stop`.
- Placement policy: legs are placed as reduce-only limit children on the entry's **first fill**, not at bracket creation, so the exchange never holds reduce-only orders against a non-existent position.
- Rounding: each leg floored to `qty_step`; the **remainder goes to the last leg**; legs that round below `min_order_qty` are merged into the adjacent leg; if no viable split exists the ladder is refused with error `LADDER_NOT_SPLITTABLE` and the response carries a single-target alternative.
- Stop resizing: when a TP leg fills, the native stop quantity is amended down to the remaining position through the shared write path, with `tpsl_mode="partial"`.
- Validation: ladder percentages must sum to <=100% (SCR-064 message "Ladder totals 110% — reduce a step.").
- Persistence and restart reconciliation; audit `position.tp_ladder_set`.

## Out of scope
- The SCR-064 / SCR-069 UI (E32-S07 / E32-S05), scaled **entries** (E32-S03), trailing (E32-S04), emulated OCO racing (E33).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A three-step ladder is placed correctly
  Given a filled long of 1.0 BTC and a ladder of 25% at 1R, 25% at 2R and 50% at 3R
  When the ladder is applied
  Then three reduce-only limit orders are placed with quantities floored to the lot size, the remainder assigned to the last leg so the quantities sum exactly to 1.0 BTC, and an audit row position.tp_ladder_set is written

Scenario: A filled leg resizes the stop
  Given the 1R leg for 0.25 BTC fills
  Then the native stop quantity is amended to 0.75 BTC in a single trading-stop call carrying both sides, and the bracket detail shows the remaining ladder

Scenario: The position is too small to split (error)
  Given a position of 0.003 BTC and a three-step ladder whose smallest leg would be below the minimum order quantity
  When the ladder is requested
  Then it is refused with LADDER_NOT_SPLITTABLE, the explanation names the instrument minimum and the offending leg, and a single-target alternative at the furthest leg's price is offered

Scenario: Percentages exceed the position (error)
  Given a ladder whose steps total 110%
  Then the request is rejected with a validation error naming the total, and no orders are placed

Scenario: Restart with a partially filled ladder (edge)
  Given the backend restarts after the 1R leg filled and before the stop resize was acknowledged
  When it comes back
  Then ladder state is restored from Postgres, the remaining position is recomputed from executions, the stop resize is re-sent with the original idempotency key, and no duplicate TP order is created

Scenario: Position flattened manually while the ladder rests (edge)
  Given I flatten the position by hand
  Then all resting ladder legs are cancelled as orphans within one 30-second reconciliation cycle with reason "position flat"
```

## Technical notes / design
- R-multiple resolution: `price = avg_entry +/- r * (avg_entry - initial_stop)` signed by side, using the **initial** stop recorded by E32-S01 so later tightening does not shift the ladder.
- `tpsl_mode` selection: exactly one leg covering 100% -> Bybit `Full` attached TP; otherwise `Partial` with reduce-only children (section 8.9 mapping table).
- Merging rule when a leg rounds below the minimum: merge **into the adjacent further leg**, preserving the trader's intent to keep the furthest target largest; record the merge in the response so the UI can show what actually got placed.
- Stop resize uses the same `TrailingTranslator.write_stop()` path as E32-S04/T03 (both sides in one call, ratcheted) — no second write path.
- Every leg carries its own deterministic `order_link_id` derived from `(trade_group_id, leg_index)`.

## Test plan
- **Unit (>=90%):** rounding and remainder assignment across many position sizes and lot steps; merge rule; refusal case; R-multiple resolution for long and short; percentage validation; stop-resize quantity maths.
- **Property test:** for random position sizes and ladder splits, assert placed quantities sum exactly to the position and no leg is below the minimum.
- **Contract:** `TakeProfitLeg` and `LADDER_NOT_SPLITTABLE` in the OpenAPI surface.
- **Integration:** recorded fixtures for leg fill -> stop resize, manual flatten -> orphan cancel, restart mid-ladder.
- **E2E:** via SCR-064 in E32-Q04.

## Security notes
Order placement path — `security` handling per section 8 of the DoR/DoD. Threat: a ladder request with 50 legs used to burn the rate budget so a protective order cannot be placed — mitigated by the ladder leg cap and by `reserved_for_protective` (section 8.7), with ladder traffic tagged `priority="normal"` and never `critical`. All mutations audited.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend. Ladder presentation as a real table is specified for SCR-064 in E32-S07.

## Performance notes
Ladder placement is batched; total placement time for a 5-leg ladder must stay inside budget #4's per-request allowance with the batch counted as one request. Stop resize on a leg fill within 500 ms of the execution event.

## Observability
`oms_tp_ladder_legs_total{result}`, `oms_tp_ladder_refused_total{reason}`, `oms_stop_resize_seconds`. Audit `position.tp_ladder_set`, `position.stop_modified{reason=ladder_fill}`.

title: Generate and submit scaled entry ladders and DCA ladders with a shared stop
body:
## Context
Two Should-stories share one engine. `US-ALGO-004` (scaled entry orders) wants a size split across N price levels with equal/linear/geometric distribution, partial-placement failure that keeps the placed legs and retries only the failed one, and group cancellation that leaves any filled portion with its protective orders intact. `US-ALGO-009` (DCA / scale-in safety ladders) adds a size multiplier, a **shared stop**, refusal when the fully-filled ladder would exceed the account risk cap, and a concurrent-order cap that queues the rest.

`24-internal-schemas.md` section 10.6 (`ScaledParams`) specifies the maths exactly: 2..50 levels, conservative rounding, duplicate-price merge, remainder to the level nearest `price_start`, sub-minimum levels dropped and redistributed proportionally, and submission via Bybit's batch endpoint at 10 orders per request where **partial success is possible** and must be handled per-item from the batch response's `retCode`.

The critical safety subtlety in `US-ALGO-009`'s NFR: *"projected risk computed for the fully-filled ladder, never for the first leg alone."*

## Scope / Deliverables
- Stories: `US-ALGO-004`, `US-ALGO-009`.
- `services/oms/algos/scaled.py` — `ScaledSupervisor` (module M14) implementing `AlgoSpec{kind="scaled"}` / `ScaledParams`.
- Pure ladder generator `generate_levels(params, instrument) -> tuple[Level, ...]`: price spacing, weight computation (`equal`, `linear` and `geometric` with `skew`, `custom` normalised weights), conservative rounding, duplicate-price merge, remainder to the level nearest `price_start`, sub-minimum drop-and-redistribute.
- DCA mode: levels expressed as percentage offsets from a reference price with a size multiplier; **one shared stop** covering the whole ladder rather than one stop per level; projected average entry, total position and total risk computed for the **fully-filled** ladder.
- Risk-cap integration (E39): the projected fully-filled risk is checked against the account cap before any order is sent; on breach the ladder is refused with the projected risk and the cap both stated.
- Concurrent-order cap: at most `max_concurrent_legs` resting at once; the remainder queues and is placed as earlier legs fill, with the queue exposed on the `trade_groups` topic.
- Batch submission at 10 orders/request with per-item `retCode` handling; failed legs recorded with their own error codes and individually retryable via `POST /api/v1/trade-groups/{tradeGroupId}/amend`.
- Group cancel via `POST /api/v1/trade-groups/{tradeGroupId}/cancel` -> `cancel-batch`, leaving any filled portion and its protective orders intact.
- Preview endpoint support: `POST /api/v1/trade-groups/preview` returns the generated ladder plus the projected rate-limit cost, so SCR-065 can show the table before anything is sent.
- Native SL: every level passes through E32-T01; DCA's shared stop is attached to the resulting position and re-sized as legs fill.
- Audit `algo.scaled_created`, `algo.scaled_cancelled`, `algo.scaled_partially_cancelled`.

## Out of scope
- The SCR-065 UI (E32-S06), TWAP/iceberg slicing (E33), multi-account fan-out of a ladder (E34), the risk-cap mechanism itself (E39).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A linear ladder is generated and placed
  Given 5 orders between 63,000 and 62,500 with linear distribution and a total of 1.0 BTC
  When the ladder is submitted
  Then five limit orders are placed with sizes per the linear weights, quantities summing exactly to 1.0 BTC with the remainder on the level nearest the start price, and a single group summary is returned

Scenario: Partial batch placement is surfaced and individually retryable (error)
  Given the third leg is rejected by the batch response with its own retCode
  Then the four placed orders remain working, the failure is reported with the exchange reason against that leg, the group is marked partially placed, and I can retry only the failed leg without disturbing the others

Scenario: Cancelling the group preserves the filled portion
  Given two of five legs have filled
  When I cancel the group
  Then all unfilled legs are cancelled, the filled position remains with its protective orders intact and still natively stopped, and algo.scaled_partially_cancelled is audited

Scenario: A DCA ladder that breaches the risk cap is refused (failure)
  Given a three-step DCA ladder at -0.5%, -1.0% and -1.8% with a 1.5 size multiplier whose fully-filled risk exceeds the account cap
  When it is requested
  Then it is refused before any order is sent, the response states the projected fully-filled risk and the cap it exceeds, and no partial ladder is placed

Scenario: Levels below the minimum lot are redistributed, not silently dropped (edge)
  Given a ladder whose levels 4 and 5 would round below the instrument minimum order quantity
  Then those levels are dropped, their quantity is redistributed proportionally to the surviving levels, the response names which levels were dropped and why, and if no viable ladder remains the request is refused with a single-order alternative

Scenario: The concurrent-leg cap queues the rest (edge)
  Given a 10-level ladder with a concurrent cap of 3
  Then exactly three legs rest at once, the remaining seven are visible as queued on the trade_groups topic, and each queued leg is placed as an earlier one fills

Scenario: Duplicate prices after rounding are merged (edge)
  Given a narrow price range where two levels round to the same tick
  Then the two levels are merged into one order with their quantities summed, so the ladder never contains two orders at the same price
```

## Technical notes / design
- The generator is a **pure function** with no I/O so the same code runs in the preview endpoint and in submission — SCR-065's preview table and the placed orders can never disagree.
- Weights per section 10.6: `equal` -> `1/n`; `linear` -> weight `i` scaled by `skew` (>1 weights the far end, <1 the near end); `geometric` -> `skew^i`; `custom` -> normalised `custom_weights` whose length must equal `levels`.
- Rounding is **conservative** (floor to `qty_step`, prices to `tickSize` away from the market for entries) so a ladder never exceeds the requested total.
- Batch transport: `submit_mode="batched"`, `batch_size=10` (Bybit's cap); the response is processed per item, and a whole-request failure is distinguished from per-item failures.
- Risk projection for DCA: `projected_qty = sum(level_qty)`, `projected_avg = weighted mean`, `projected_risk = projected_qty * |projected_avg - shared_stop|`, checked against E39's cap for the account. This is the fully-filled figure the NFR demands.
- Rate-limit awareness: the preview returns the projected request count; submission tags legs `priority="normal"` so they can never consume the protective reserve.
- Cross-check with `instruments-info` precision filters (`priceFilter`, `lotSizeFilter`) supplied by E28's validation layer.

## Test plan
- **Unit (>=90%):** each distribution's weights; skew behaviour; rounding and remainder placement; duplicate merge; sub-minimum drop and redistribution; the no-viable-ladder refusal; DCA multiplier and projected-risk maths; concurrent-cap queueing.
- **Property tests:** placed quantities always sum to the requested total (or the request is refused); no level below the minimum ever reaches the adapter; no two levels share a price.
- **Contract:** `AlgoSpec.scaled`, `/trade-groups/preview` response, per-leg error shape.
- **Integration:** recorded fixtures — batch partial success, whole-batch rejection, `10018` rate-limit mid-ladder, leg fill during queueing.
- **E2E:** via SCR-065 in E32-Q04.
- Fixtures: `tests/fixtures/bybit/batch_partial_success.json`, `batch_rate_limited.json`.

## Security notes
Order placement path (`security` label mandatory). Threats: **DoS** — a 50-level ladder saturating the order-create bucket so a stop cannot be placed, mitigated by the level cap, the `normal` priority class and `reserved_for_protective`; **tampering** — a preview computed client-side diverging from what is submitted, mitigated by the shared pure generator and server-side re-computation at submit time (the client's preview is never trusted); **elevation** — account scope checked per leg. All group mutations audited with the full parameter set per SCR-065's audit spec.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend. The preview table contract exists specifically so SCR-065 can render an accessible real table (E32-S06).

## Performance notes
Preview generation must complete in <=5 ms server-side so SCR-065 can recompute within one frame. Submission of a 50-level ladder is 5 batch requests; total submit->ack p95 must stay inside budget #4 per request, and the ladder must not push the account over its per-UID budget (checked before the first request is sent).

## Observability

Audit `algo.scaled_created` with `{symbol, side, levels, totalQty, priceRange, distribution, accountIds, environment}`, `algo.scaled_cancelled`, `algo.scaled_partially_cancelled`.

## Definition of Done

title: Translate percentage and ATR trailing stops into Bybit price distances
body:
## Context
`US-ALGO-008` (**Must**) wants fixed-distance and percentage trailing stops, using "the native Bybit trailing stop where possible", with percentage trails translated to a price distance and maintained client-side with the translation shown, and app-managed trails restored from the database within 5 seconds of a restart.

The hard constraint is in `24-internal-schemas.md` section 8.9: Bybit's `trading-stop.trailingStop` is a **price distance, not a percentage**. Section 10.7's `TrailSpec` adds the binding rule `only_tighten: bool = True  # ratchet — binding, cannot be set False`. And the same section records the trap that one-sided TP/SL modification via `trading-stop` breaks Bybit's OCO pairing, so **both** sides must be written in every call, sending the unchanged side's current value explicitly.

`20-architecture.md` section 9 rule 6 places this translation in the OMS, never in the UI — so that chart drags (E31), the ticket (E30), SCR-064 (E32-S07) and rule-engine trails (E35) all share one implementation and one ratchet.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Stories: `US-ALGO-008`.
- `services/oms/algos/trailing.py` — `TrailingTranslator` (module M14), owning the **single** `trading-stop` write path for the whole product: `write_stop(position, *, stop=None, take_profit=None, trailing=None, reason, actor)`.
- Translation of `TrailSpec{kind: fixed_ticks|percent|atr|structure|ma, value, atr_period, swing_lookback, activation_r, only_tighten, update_on}` into the Bybit request: `fixed_ticks` and `percent` map to the **native** `trailingStop` distance; `atr`, `structure` and `ma` are computed per bar and pushed as `trading-stop` updates.
- Both-sides write rule enforced structurally: the function always sends the current value of the side it is not changing.
- Ratchet: any write that would loosen the stop is refused, counted and logged; `only_tighten=False` is rejected at the type boundary (it is not settable through the API).
- Activation: `activation_r` arms the trail only after that R-multiple is reached, using the frozen initial stop from E32-S01.
- App-managed trail state persisted per position; on restart, trails resume within **5 seconds** and the gap is logged, per the story's NFR.
- Percentage translation is surfaced: the API response and the `positions` topic carry both the user's unit/value and the resulting absolute distance and trigger price, so the UI can show "1.5% = 958 USDT distance, trigger 62,942".
- Labelling: app-managed (ATR/structure/MA) trails are flagged `managed_by="engine"` on the wire so CMP-227 EstimatedBadge / CMP-158 can render the distinction.

## Out of scope
- ATR/structure/MA **computation rules** authored by users (E35 rule engine supplies the signal; this story supplies the write path and the ratchet), break-even (E32-T03), the SCR-064 UI (E32-S07).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A percentage trail becomes a native price distance
  Given a 1.5% trailing stop on a long position at an entry of 63,900
  When the trail is armed
  Then the OMS computes the absolute quote-currency distance, submits it as trailingStop via POST /v5/position/trading-stop in a call that also carries the current take-profit value, and the API response and positions topic report both the 1.5% input and the resulting distance and trigger price

Scenario: A fixed-distance trail uses the native field directly
  Given a 150 USDT trail on a long
  Then the native Bybit trailing stop is used with that distance and the current trigger price is shown, with no engine-managed state required

Scenario: A loosening update is refused (failure)
  Given an armed trail whose recomputed distance would move the stop further from the mark
  When the update is evaluated
  Then the write is refused, oms_stop_loosening_refused_total increments, the existing stop is unchanged, and the refusal is logged with the attempted and current values

Scenario: An app-managed trail survives a restart
  Given an engine-managed ATR trail is running and the backend restarts
  When it comes back
  Then trail state is restored from Postgres, trailing resumes within 5 seconds, the gap duration is logged, and the position's native stop was never removed during the gap

Scenario: A one-sided write is structurally impossible (edge)
  Given any caller updating only the stop-loss side
  When write_stop executes
  Then the request still carries the position's current take-profit value explicitly, so Bybit's TP/SL pairing is preserved, asserted by a test that inspects the outgoing request

Scenario: An explicit user override to loosen is audited (edge)
  Given the user explicitly confirms loosening the stop through the audited override path
  Then the write proceeds, an audit row with reason "user_override_loosen" and the actor is written, and a warning-level log records the previous and new values
```

## Technical notes / design
- `write_stop()` is the single call site of `adapter.set_trading_stop` — enforced by an architecture test mirroring E32-T01's `place_order` test, so no future feature can add a second, unratcheted write path.
- Percent-to-distance conversion uses the **position's average entry** as the reference for the initial distance and the running extreme (highest-high for longs, lowest-low for shorts) for subsequent updates; the reference used is recorded on every update for auditability.
- Rounding: the computed distance is rounded to `tickSize` in the **tightening** direction so rounding can never loosen.
- `update_on="bar_close"` (default) versus `"tick"`: bar-close updates are driven by the bar builder (M7); tick updates are rate-limited to the account's amend budget with `priority="normal"`.
- Engine-managed trails are stored with their spec and last-applied distance so a restart recomputes rather than re-derives from scratch.
- Native versus engine selection is capability-driven (`ExchangeCapabilities.supports_native_trailing`, section 14/10.8) rather than `if exchange == "bybit"`.

## Test plan
- **Unit (>=90%):** percent/ATR/tick conversions for long and short; tightening-direction rounding; ratchet refusal; activation-R gating; both-sides payload construction; restart state restoration.
- **Architecture test:** single call site of `adapter.set_trading_stop`.
- **Property test:** for random sequences of price moves and updates, the stop distance from the extreme is monotonically non-increasing.
- **Contract:** `TrailingStopSpec` in the OpenAPI surface; `positions` payload carrying unit, value, distance, trigger and `managed_by`.
- **Integration:** recorded fixtures for trading-stop acceptance, rejection, and the pairing behaviour observed in E32-K01.
- **Chaos:** restart with an engine trail armed (E32-Q05), asserting the 5-second resume.

## Security notes
A bug that loosens a stop is a **P0 safety defect**. Controls: the ratchet is enforced in the single write path, `only_tighten` is not settable to false through any API, the loosening override requires explicit user confirmation and writes an audit row naming the actor, and the architecture test prevents a bypass path from being added. RBAC `positions:write` plus account scope. Security-engineer review required.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend. The requirement that the translation is *shown* is satisfied by the wire contract above and rendered by CMP-120 in E32-S07.

## Performance notes
Translation must add <=1 ms per update. Bar-close updates are naturally rate-limited; tick-mode updates must respect the amend budget and never starve protective traffic (section 8.7).

## Observability
`oms_trailing_updates_total{kind,managed_by}`, `oms_stop_loosening_refused_total{reason}`, `oms_trailing_resume_seconds` (restart gap). Audit `position.stop_modified{reason=trail|user_override_loosen}`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All scenarios automated, including the architecture test and the monotonicity property test.
- [ ] Coverage >=90% on M14.
- [ ] Schema delta for sections 8.9/10.7 drafted for E32-T04.
- [ ] Security-engineer review comment present.
- [ ] Restart-resume measured at <=5 s.
