title: Build the SCR-069 bracket builder with a non-removable native stop floor
body:
## Context
`SCR-069` "Emulated OCO / bracket builder" is a modal offering an entry plus its exit pair, explicitly labelled where emulation applies, and — the part this epic owns — showing **"the mandatory native SL floor that remains regardless"**. Its design sign-off checklist requires: entry+bracket and standalone-OCO variants drawn, the emulation caveat stated prominently, race-resolution behaviour explained, the residual-risk state drawn, *"the mandatory native SL floor is shown as always-present and non-removable"*, and validation messages drawn.

E32 builds the **bracket half** (entry + native SL + TP or TP ladder). E33 adds the standalone-OCO half into the same modal shell. The shared shell, including the CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice and the native-SL floor affordance, is built here so E33 extends rather than duplicates.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Stories: `US-ALGO-001` (UI half), `US-ALGO-003` (ladder entry UI half).
- Screen `SCR-069`; components `CMP-043` Dialog, `CMP-100` PriceInput, `CMP-101` QtyInput, `CMP-119` BracketEditor, `CMP-158` SafetyInvariantNotice, `CMP-118` AlgoProgressCard, `CMP-227` EstimatedBadge.
- `apps/web/src/features/algo/BracketBuilder/` — modal shell, entry section, stop section, take-profit section (single target or ladder), preview summary, submit.
- The stop field is **always present and cannot be cleared**: attempting to empty it restores the profile default and shows the CMP-158 note "Every position keeps a native stop — you can move it, not delete it."
- Price entry modes: absolute price, ticks from entry, percent, and R-multiple, with the others recomputed live (per SCR-064's checklist, shared behaviour in CMP-119).
- Resulting risk shown in account currency and in R **before** confirm.
- Validation surfaces: side correctness, beyond-liquidation stop, ladder totals >100%, `LADDER_NOT_SPLITTABLE` from E32-S02 with its single-target alternative offered as a one-click action.
- States: empty, editing, validating, submitting (per-child progress), submitted, partial-placement failure with retry, error.
- Submits via `POST /api/v1/orders` with `algo.bracket`; tracks group state from the `orders` / `trade_groups` WS topics.
- Analytics/audit hooks per the screen spec; `EstimatedBadge` on anything engine-managed.

## Out of scope
- The standalone-OCO variant and its race-resolution copy (E33), the scaled builder (E32-S06), SCR-064 (E32-S07), the order ticket itself (E30).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A bracket is built and submitted
  Given the modal is open for BTCUSDT with an entry price, a stop and a single take-profit
  When I submit
  Then one bracket group is created, per-child progress is shown while it places, and on success the modal closes with the group visible in the orders panel

Scenario: The native stop cannot be removed
  Given the modal is open
  When I clear the stop-loss field
  Then the field repopulates with the profile default, the CMP-158 note "Every position keeps a native stop - you can move it, not delete it." is shown as a persistent role="note", and the submit button remains enabled with a valid stop

Scenario: Risk is restated before confirmation
  Given an entry, a stop and a quantity
  Then the resulting risk is shown in account currency and as an R-multiple, updating live as any input changes, and the submit button names the action and the risk

Scenario: An unsplittable ladder offers its alternative (error)
  Given I configure a three-step take-profit ladder the backend refuses with LADDER_NOT_SPLITTABLE
  Then the error names the instrument minimum and the offending leg, and a one-click "use a single target instead" action reconfigures the form without losing my other inputs

Scenario: A stop on the wrong side is blocked (edge)
  Given a long entry at 63,000 and a stop entered at 63,500
  Then an inline validation message explains that a long's stop must be below the entry, the submit control is disabled, and no request is sent

Scenario: Partial placement is shown honestly (failure)
  Given the entry places but a ladder child is rejected
  Then the modal shows which children placed and which failed with the exchange reason, offers a retry limited to the failed child, and does not imply the whole bracket succeeded
```

## Technical notes / design
- Build against the handoff pack from `E32-D07`; component behaviour contracts come from `15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-119 and CMP-158.
- All price-mode recomputation is local and synchronous; the authoritative validation is still the backend's, and the UI never places an order the backend has not validated.
- The preview never computes the ladder itself: it calls `POST /api/v1/trade-groups/preview` so the displayed table is produced by the same pure generator that will submit (E32-S03's rule, applied here to bracket ladders too).
- Optimistic UI is forbidden for protective state: a stop is rendered "pending" until the exchange acknowledges (SCR-064's performance note, applied consistently).
- Modal shell is extracted as `AlgoBuilderDialog` so E33 mounts its OCO variant into it without forking.
- Storybook stories for every enumerated state, including partial-placement failure.

## Test plan
- **Unit/component (>=80% frontend):** price-mode recomputation; stop-cannot-be-cleared behaviour; risk restatement; validation messages; state machine across all enumerated states.
- **Contract:** the request shape matches `AlgoSpec.bracket` in the OpenAPI schema (typed client generated from it).
- **E2E (Playwright, web + Electron):** build and submit a bracket on demo; attempt to clear the stop; unsplittable-ladder alternative; partial-placement retry — added in E32-Q04.
- **a11y:** axe-core on every state; keyboard-only submission; screen-reader pass on the CMP-158 note and the validation messages.
- **Visual regression:** Storybook snapshots per state.

## Security notes
This surface can place orders, so it inherits `security` handling. The UI enforces nothing security-relevant on its own — all invariants are server-side (E32-T01) — and the abuse case "a crafted client request strips the stop" is verified in E32-X02 against the API, not the UI. No secrets touch the client; account scope comes from the session.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA. The CMP-158 native-SL guarantee is a persistent `role="note"`, never a tooltip or toast. Every numeric input is labelled with its unit. The submit button names the full action ("Place bracket: buy 0.25 BTC, stop 62,800, target 64,450"). R-multiples and percentages are both present as text. Focus is trapped in the modal, returns to the invoking control on close, and the first error is announced and focused on failed validation. Every drag-equivalent interaction has a keyboard path.

## Performance notes
Input recomputation within one frame (<=16.6 ms). Submission inherits budget #4; the UI shows "placing" immediately and never blocks the main thread on the response.

## Observability
Analytics `algo.bracket_previewed`, `algo.bracket_field_changed`; audit events are emitted server-side. Client error boundary reports failed submissions with the correlation id from the API response.

title: Build the SCR-065 scaled and DCA ladder builder with a full preview table
body:
## Context
`SCR-065` "Scaled / ladder order builder" is the modal that splits size across N orders between two prices with equal/linear/geometric distribution and a **preview table of every child order**. Its spec fixes the validation rules (2-50 child orders; each child >= min lot, with the message "Child 5 is below the minimum — reduce the order count"; a range crossing the mark is a warning, not a block), the states (preview, placing with per-child progress, partial placement failure with retry), and the a11y requirement that the generated ladder is previewed as a **real table** with level, price, qty, cumulative qty, cumulative notional and resulting average, with a submit button that names the total ("Place 8 orders, 0.64 BTC total").

Its performance note is explicit: preview recomputes locally within one frame, and submission fans the levels out in a **single backend request** so the per-account rate-limit budget is evaluated server-side and reported back before any order is sent. The screen also demands the mandatory native SL be drawn explicitly, per level or per resulting position.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Stories: `US-ALGO-004` (UI half), `US-ALGO-009` (UI half).
- Screen `SCR-065`; components `CMP-010` Slider, `CMP-043` Dialog, `CMP-049` Table, `CMP-100` PriceInput, `CMP-101` QtyInput, `CMP-119` BracketEditor, `CMP-130` SlippageEstimateChip, `CMP-228` PreviewTile, `CMP-158` SafetyInvariantNotice.
- `apps/web/src/features/algo/ScaledBuilder/` — generator inputs (from price, to price, order count, total qty, distribution, skew, reduce-only, TIF), DCA mode (percent offsets, size multiplier, shared stop), the preview table, the rate-limit estimate, and submit.
- Preview is fetched from `POST /api/v1/trade-groups/preview` so the table is generated by the same server-side pure generator that submits (never a client re-implementation), with a local optimistic recompute for slider responsiveness that is always reconciled against the server result before submit is enabled.
- Preview table columns: level, price, qty, cumulative qty, cumulative notional, resulting average entry.
- Summary tiles (CMP-228): total quantity, average entry, total notional, projected risk for the **fully-filled** ladder versus the account cap, and the projected request count as a share of the minute budget.
- Native SL affordance: the shared stop (DCA) or per-position stop is shown as always-present and non-removable via CMP-158.
- Validation surfaces: 2-50 levels; sub-minimum child message; range-crosses-mark warning; risk-cap refusal from E32-S03 restated with projected risk and cap.
- States: preview, placing (per-child progress), partial placement failure with per-leg retry, cancelled, error.
- Analytics/audit per the screen spec: `algo.scaled_previewed`, `algo.scaled_distribution_changed` (analytics); server emits the audited events.

## Out of scope
- The ladder maths itself (E32-S03 owns it server-side), TWAP/iceberg builders (E33), SCR-064 (E32-S07), multi-account fan-out selection (E34).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The preview table matches what gets placed
  Given 5 orders between 63,900 and 63,700 with linear distribution, skew 1.4 and a total of 1.00 BTC
  When the preview renders
  Then a real table shows level, price, qty, cumulative qty, cumulative notional and the resulting average for each of the five children, and submitting places exactly those orders

Scenario: The submit control names the whole action
  Given a valid 8-level ladder totalling 0.64 BTC
  Then the submit button reads "Place 8 orders, 0.64 BTC total" and the rate-limit estimate is shown before submission

Scenario: A child below the minimum lot is explained (error)
  Given an order count that would push child 5 below the instrument minimum
  Then the message "Child 5 is below the minimum - reduce the order count" is shown inline, submission is blocked, and the offending row is marked in the table

Scenario: A range that crosses the mark warns without blocking (edge)
  Given a buy ladder whose upper price is above the current mark
  Then a warning is shown explaining the immediate-fill consequence, and submission remains possible

Scenario: A DCA ladder over the risk cap is refused with numbers (failure)
  Given a DCA ladder whose fully-filled risk exceeds the account cap
  When I submit
  Then the refusal states the projected fully-filled risk and the cap it exceeds, the ladder is not placed, and my inputs are preserved so I can reduce size

Scenario: Partial placement offers a per-leg retry (failure)
  Given three of five legs place and two are rejected
  Then the table marks each leg placed or failed with the exchange reason, a retry action is offered for the failed legs only, and cancelling the group leaves any filled portion with its protective orders intact
```

## Technical notes / design
- The local recompute exists only for slider smoothness; a `previewToken` from the server response gates the submit button, so a stale local preview can never be submitted.
- Table is virtualised at 50 rows (trivially, but consistently with CMP-049's contract) and remains a real `<table>` with header associations for screen readers.
- Rate-limit estimate comes from the preview response, not a client guess.
- Slider and numeric inputs stay in sync bidirectionally; the distribution selector changes only weights, never the price bounds.
- Storybook stories for all states including partial failure and risk-cap refusal.

## Test plan
- **Unit/component (>=80%):** input binding and slider sync; preview token gating; validation messages; per-leg retry state; DCA mode inputs.
- **Contract:** preview request/response against `/trade-groups/preview` in `22-api-openapi.yaml`.
- **E2E (Playwright web + Electron):** generate, preview, submit, partial-failure retry, risk-cap refusal — added in E32-Q04.
- **a11y:** axe-core on every state; table semantics verified with a screen reader; keyboard-only generation and submission.
- **Perf:** preview interaction measured within one frame.

## Security notes
Order-placing surface, `security` handling. The client's preview is advisory only — the server regenerates and revalidates at submit time (E32-S03), so a tampered client preview cannot place a different ladder. The rate-limit estimate is informational; enforcement is server-side. Account scope from the session; no secrets client-side.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA. The ladder preview is a real table with row and column headers, not a styled grid of divs. Every generator input is a labelled numeric field with its unit. The submit button names the total order count and quantity. The CMP-158 native-SL note is a persistent `role="note"`. Warnings (range crosses mark) use `role="status"`; blocking errors use `role="alert"` and move focus to the first offending field. Slider controls have keyboard equivalents and expose value text.

## Performance notes
Preview recomputes within one frame (<=16.6 ms) per the screen spec. Submission is a single backend request regardless of level count. The table must not re-render every row on a single-input change (memoised rows).

## Observability
Analytics `algo.scaled_previewed`, `algo.scaled_distribution_changed`. Audited events are server-emitted (`algo.scaled_created` etc.). Failed submissions report the API correlation id.

- [ ] All scenarios automated; Storybook covers every state.

title: Build the SCR-064 position SL/TP editor with trailing, break-even and TP ladder
body:
## Context
`SCR-064` "Position SL/TP editor (modal)" is the single surface where a trader manages an existing position's protection: stop-loss with its trigger source, a take-profit ladder with per-step native flags, a trailing stop (fixed offset / % / ATR multiple / structure-based) marked only-tighten, a break-even trigger in R, and — crucially — **which of these are native exchange-side versus engine-managed**, with the standing note "Engine-managed stops need the backend online. A native stop at 63,900 always remains."

Its validation rules are fixed by the screen spec: SL/TP side correctness; ladder percentages sum <=100% ("Ladder totals 110% — reduce a step."); each ladder step >= min lot; and the native-SL invariant cannot be removed ("Every position keeps a native stop — you can move it, not delete it."). Its sign-off checklist demands price/ticks/%/R-multiple entry modes recomputing live, resulting risk in account currency and R before confirm, invalid-side and beyond-liquidation validation, the partial-quantity TP ladder variant, and **a keyboard path equivalent to chart drag-to-modify**.

This story consumes three backend behaviours built earlier in the epic: TP ladders (E32-S02), trailing translation (E32-S04) and break-even (E32-T03).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Stories: `US-ALGO-008` (UI half), `US-ALGO-003` (position-side ladder UI).
- Screen `SCR-064`; components `CMP-001` Button, `CMP-043` Dialog, `CMP-100` PriceInput, `CMP-119` BracketEditor, `CMP-120` TrailingStopEditor, `CMP-130` SlippageEstimateChip, `CMP-158` SafetyInvariantNotice.
- `apps/web/src/features/positions/SlTpEditor/` — stop section with trigger source (Last/Mark/Index, defaulting to Mark), TP ladder section with per-step percentage and native flag, trailing section (CMP-120), break-even section, native-versus-engine labelling, apply.
- Entry modes: price, ticks, percent and R-multiple, with the others recomputed live; resulting risk in account currency and R shown before confirm.
- Trailing display: the user's unit and value **and** the translated absolute distance and trigger price, sourced from E32-S04's response contract — the UI performs no translation of its own.
- Pending semantics: a changed SL/TP renders as **pending** until the exchange acknowledges, never optimistically as confirmed.
- Native-SL floor: the stop cannot be removed; clearing it restores the current value with the CMP-158 message.
- Writes via `PUT /api/v1/positions/{positionId}/tpsl`, always sending both sides (the backend enforces this; the UI's form model reflects it so the user sees both values being written).
- States: loading, editing, validating, pending-acknowledgement, applied, rejected with the exchange reason, position-closed-while-editing.
- Keyboard equivalence to chart drag-to-modify: every adjustment reachable and performable from the keyboard with announced values.

## Out of scope
- Chart drag-to-modify itself (E31), the bracket builder (E32-S05), the scaled builder (E32-S06), rule-authored trails (E35).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A percentage trail shows its translation
  Given a long position and a 1.5% trailing stop
  When I apply it
  Then the editor shows the 1.5% input alongside the translated absolute distance and resulting trigger price returned by the backend, labels the trail as native or engine-managed, and renders the change as pending until Bybit acknowledges

Scenario: The stop cannot be deleted
  Given the editor is open on a protected position
  When I clear the stop-loss field
  Then the previous value is restored and the persistent note "Every position keeps a native stop - you can move it, not delete it." is shown, and no request removing the stop is ever sent

Scenario: A ladder totalling more than the position is blocked (error)
  Given ladder steps of 25%, 25% and 60%
  Then the inline message "Ladder totals 110% - reduce a step." is shown, apply is disabled, and the offending step is marked

Scenario: An engine-managed trail is labelled with its residual risk
  Given an ATR-based trail, which has no native equivalent
  Then it is labelled engine-managed with the standing note that engine-managed stops need the backend online while the native stop at its current price always remains, presented as persistent text rather than a tooltip

Scenario: The exchange rejects the amend (failure)
  Given Bybit rejects the trading-stop write
  Then the pending state resolves to rejected with the exchange reason shown verbatim plus a plain-language explanation, the previous values are restored in the form, and the position's existing protection is stated explicitly so I know what is currently in force

Scenario: The position closes while the editor is open (edge)
  Given the position is flattened elsewhere while I am editing
  Then the editor switches to a closed state explaining that the position no longer exists, disables apply, and offers to close the modal without sending anything

Scenario: Every adjustment is keyboard-reachable (edge)
  Given keyboard-only operation
  Then each of stop, each ladder step, the trail and the break-even trigger can be focused, adjusted in the current entry mode and applied, with the resulting risk announced, matching what chart drag-to-modify can do
```

## Technical notes / design
- Built against E32-D07's handoff pack; CMP-120 TrailingStopEditor's behaviour contract comes from `15-component-catalogue.md`.
- The form model always carries both TP and SL current values so the both-sides write rule (section 8.9) is visible to the user rather than a hidden backend detail.
- R-multiple mode resolves against the position's frozen initial stop, matching the backend's computation (E32-S01), so the UI and the OMS never disagree about what 1R means.
- Beyond-liquidation validation uses the liquidation price from the `positions` topic; if unavailable, the check degrades to a warning rather than a false block.
- Pending state is driven by the `positions` topic acknowledgement, not by the HTTP response alone.
- Storybook stories for every state including rejected and position-closed.

## Test plan
- **Unit/component (>=80%):** entry-mode recomputation across price/ticks/percent/R; ladder total validation; stop-not-removable behaviour; pending/rejected/closed state machine; native-versus-engine labelling.
- **Contract:** `PUT /positions/{positionId}/tpsl` request/response and the `positions` payload fields (`managed_by`, `breakeven_armed`, translated distance).
- **E2E (Playwright web + Electron):** apply a percentage trail; attempt to clear the stop; ladder-total error; exchange rejection; position-closed-while-editing — added in E32-Q04.
- **a11y:** axe-core all states; full keyboard-equivalence script; screen-reader pass on the engine-managed note and on pending/rejected transitions.

## Security notes
Mutates protective state on a live (demo) position, so `security` handling applies. The UI cannot weaken protection: removal is impossible client-side and refused server-side (E32-T01/S04's ratchet), and any loosening override goes through the audited backend path with explicit confirmation. RBAC `positions:write`; the editor is read-only for the `viewer` role. No secrets client-side.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA, and this screen carries two explicit standing requirements from the catalogue: R-multiples and percentages are both shown, and the warning about engine-managed stops is a persistent, readable note rather than a tooltip. Additionally: keyboard equivalence to chart drag-to-modify is a first-class acceptance criterion; pending and rejected transitions are announced via `role="status"` / `role="alert"`; every numeric field is labelled with its unit; focus returns to the invoking position row on close.

## Performance notes
Amend round-trip target <=500 ms p95 (the screen's stated budget, aligned with budget #4's amend path). Entry-mode recomputation within one frame. The new SL/TP renders pending, never optimistically confirmed.

## Observability
Analytics on entry-mode switches and trail-kind selection. Audit events (`position.stop_modified`, `position.tp_ladder_set`) are server-emitted; the client surfaces the correlation id on failure.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All scenarios automated; Storybook covers every state.
- [ ] Frontend coverage >=80%.
- [ ] axe-core green; manual screen-reader pass; the keyboard-equivalence script passes.
- [ ] design-qa comparison against the E32-D07 pack (feeds E32-D08).

title: Run UX research on bracket, ladder and mandatory-stop mental models
body:
## Context
E32 introduces three interaction models the product has never had, each with a known failure mode in trading tools: a **bracket** the user must understand as one object rather than three orders; a **generated ladder** whose child orders the user never types individually and therefore may not trust; and a **stop the system guarantees and the user may only tighten**, which is a constraint users typically experience as the app fighting them unless the rationale is visible.

The design-ahead rule (`00-planning-brief.md`; `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 3.1) requires design Done >=2 sprints before the consuming FE stories, which land in S17 — so research runs in S13. This ticket exists because SCR-064/065/069 each carry design sign-off checklists with items that cannot be answered from first principles: *what must the user see to trust a generated ladder*, and *how should a non-removable stop be expressed so it reads as protection rather than obstruction*.

## Scope / Deliverables
- 5-6 moderated sessions with the owner plus account managers matching the personas in `docs/plan/10-personas.md`, 45 minutes each.
- Stimulus: competitor bracket/ladder UIs and two paper prototypes of the non-removable stop (hard-lock versus explain-and-restore).
- Research questions: (1) Do users read a bracket as one object, and what representation makes the relationship obvious? (2) What columns and totals must a ladder preview show before users will submit it unseen? (3) How should "native exchange-side" versus "engine-managed" be expressed so the residual risk of engine-managed stops is understood? (4) Is the R-multiple or the account-currency figure the primary risk reference, and which should lead? (5) What do users expect when a stop is cleared?
- Deliverable: a findings report in `docs/design/research/e32-brackets-ladders.md` with prioritised implications, verbatim quotes, and an explicit recommendation for each of the five questions.
- A one-page "mental model" summary consumed directly by E32-D02's wireframes.

## Out of scope
- Any visual design; usability testing of built screens (that is E32-D08's design QA); emulated-algo concepts (E33's own research).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every research question is answered with evidence
  Given the sessions are complete
  When the report is published
  Then each of the five research questions has a recommendation supported by at least three participant observations, and each recommendation names the screen and checklist item it resolves

Scenario: The non-removable stop has a chosen expression
  Given both paper prototypes were tested
  Then the report recommends one of hard-lock or explain-and-restore, states the evidence, and specifies the exact copy pattern for the chosen option

Scenario: A contradicted assumption is recorded, not buried (edge)
  Given participants reject an assumption baked into the SCR-065 wireframe sketch
  Then the report states the contradiction explicitly and files a design change request against E32-D02 rather than proceeding as planned
```

## Technical notes / design

E32 owns the bracket variant and the shared shell; E33 extends it with the OCO variant, so this ticket must design the shell as extensible and hand E33 a documented extension point.

- Copy for every validation message and for the CMP-158 native-SL note, finalised with the content owner.
- The extension point for E33's OCO variant documented as an annotated frame so E33's designer does not fork the shell.
- Per-child placement progress treatment for the submitting state.
- Redlines and token references for engineering.

Each control annotated with its analytics/audit event.

`SCR-065`'s sign-off checklist requires: start/end price, level count and distribution (flat / linear / exponential / custom) drawn; the full preview table with resulting average price; the rate-limit estimate shown before submit; validation messages for tick/lot rounding and for a range crossing the mark; **the mandatory native SL applied per level or per resulting position drawn explicitly**; and a cancel-all-levels control. The screen's a11y note further requires the ladder to be previewed as a real table with level, price, qty, cumulative qty, cumulative notional and resulting average, and a submit button that names the total.

The DCA variant (`US-ALGO-009`) shares this screen and adds percent offsets, a size multiplier, a shared stop and a projected fully-filled risk figure against the account cap — which is the number that stops a trader accidentally laddering into a cap breach.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi frames for every SCR-065 state from E32-D02 (preview, placing with per-child progress, partial-placement failure with per-leg retry, risk-cap refusal, cancelled, error), light and dark, both densities.
- The scaled and DCA input variants, with the DCA-specific shared-stop and projected-risk-versus-cap treatment.
- Preview table design at 3, 10 and 50 rows, including the cumulative columns and the resulting-average row, with the per-leg status column used in the partial-failure state.
- `CMP-228 PreviewTile` usage spec for the summary tiles (total qty, average entry, total notional, projected risk vs cap, projected request count vs minute budget).
- Rate-limit estimate presentation, including the over-budget refusal state.
- Distribution control design including the `skew` slider and its live effect on the table.
- Copy for the validation messages fixed by the screen spec.

## Out of scope
- SCR-069 (E32-D03), SCR-064 (E32-D05), design-system contributions and motion (E32-D06), the ladder maths itself.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every checklist item on SCR-065 is satisfied
  Given the screen's design sign-off acceptance checklist
  When the CDO reviews
  Then every item is ticked with the frame naming it, including the explicit drawing of how the mandatory native stop applies to a laddered entry

Scenario: The preview table works at the level cap
  Given the 50-row frame
  Then the modal remains usable without nested scrolling of the summary tiles, the header row remains visible, and the resulting-average row is reachable without losing the submit control

Scenario: The risk-cap refusal explains itself with numbers (failure)
  Given a DCA ladder over the account cap
  Then the refusal state shows the projected fully-filled risk and the cap side by side, preserves the user's inputs in the frame, and offers a reduce-size affordance

Scenario: Distribution changes are legible (edge)
  Given the skew slider is moved
  Then the frames show how the table and the summary tiles respond, so engineering knows which parts re-render and which stay stable
```

## Technical notes / design
Published tokens only; CMP-049 Table's existing contract is respected rather than a bespoke grid. Progress for per-child placement reuses CMP-023's pattern rather than inventing a new one. The optimistic-local-preview-versus-server-preview distinction from E32-S06 is annotated so the designer's intent about when the submit control unlocks is unambiguous.

## Test plan
N/A — design artefact. Verification: checklist walkthrough with the CDO; contrast per frame; engineering feasibility review against the `/trade-groups/preview` contract.

## Security notes
No real account data in frames. The rate-limit estimate must be presented as informational, never as the enforcement mechanism, so users do not infer client-side authority.

## Accessibility notes
The preview must be designed as a real table with visible column headers, not a styled grid. Submit button copy names the count and total. Warning versus blocking-error treatments are visually and semantically distinct and annotated with their ARIA roles. The slider's keyboard equivalent and its value text are specified.

## Performance notes
The design must support recomputation within one frame: the annotation states which elements are memoised and which update per input event.

## Observability
Controls annotated with `algo.scaled_previewed` and `algo.scaled_distribution_changed` analytics events; audited events noted as server-emitted.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All states designed in both themes and densities, including 3/10/50-row table variants.
- [ ] CMP-228 usage spec complete.
- [ ] Every catalogue checklist item ticked with evidence.
- [ ] Contrast verified per frame.
- [ ] Engineering feasibility review recorded.
- [ ] CDO sign-off recorded (Done), >=2 sprints before E32-S06 starts.

## Context
`SCR-064` is the densest E32 surface: stop with trigger source, a partial-quantity TP ladder with per-step native flags, a trailing stop across four kinds (fixed offset / % / ATR multiple / structure), a break-even trigger in R, and the native-versus-engine-managed distinction with its standing residual-risk note. Its sign-off checklist demands price/ticks/%/R-multiple entry modes with the others recomputed live, resulting risk in account currency and R before confirm, the "SL cannot be removed, only moved" rule stated and enforced in the UI, invalid-side and beyond-liquidation validation messages, the partial-quantity TP ladder variant, and **a keyboard path equivalent to chart drag-to-modify**.

`CMP-120 TrailingStopEditor` is specified here and is the component that has to make Bybit's price-distance reality legible to a user thinking in percentages.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi frames for every SCR-064 state (loading, editing, validating, pending-acknowledgement, applied, rejected with exchange reason, position-closed-while-editing), light and dark, both densities.

- Pending-versus-confirmed visual language for protective changes — the screen forbids optimistic confirmation, so "pending" needs a design that reads as "not yet in force".
- The partial-quantity TP ladder variant with per-step native flags.
- The break-even control with its R input and fee-offset option.
- The standing engine-managed residual-risk note as persistent text (never a tooltip) with finalised copy.
- Keyboard-interaction specification mapping every chart drag-to-modify action to a keyboard equivalent on this screen.

## Out of scope
- SCR-069 (E32-D03), SCR-065 (E32-D04), chart drag-to-modify itself (E31's design), motion (E32-D06).

```gherkin
  Given a 1.5% trail on a long

Scenario: Pending never reads as confirmed (failure)
  Given a submitted change awaiting exchange acknowledgement
  Then the pending treatment is visually and textually distinct from applied, states what protection is currently in force, and is drawn alongside the rejected state so the transition is designed end to end

Scenario: Keyboard equivalence is designed, not assumed (edge)
  Given the chart drag-to-modify actions in E31
  Then this screen's spec maps each one to a keyboard-operable control here, and the mapping is reviewed by the accessibility specialist
```

## Technical notes / design
Published tokens only. The native/engine badge uses CMP-227 EstimatedBadge where the displayed value is engine-derived. The R-multiple mode's reference (the frozen initial stop) is annotated so engineering matches the backend's definition.

## Test plan
N/A — design artefact. Verification: CDO checklist walkthrough, contrast per frame, accessibility-specialist review of the keyboard mapping, engineering feasibility review against `PUT /positions/{positionId}/tpsl`.

## Security notes
The design must offer no affordance that suggests deleting protection. The loosening-override path (which exists server-side with explicit confirmation and audit) is drawn as a deliberate, friction-carrying flow, not a casual toggle.

## Accessibility notes
This is the screen with the most demanding a11y requirements in E32: both R and percentage shown as text; the engine-managed warning as persistent readable text; keyboard equivalence to chart drag-to-modify; announced pending/rejected transitions. All are annotated on the frames with roles and focus order, and reviewed by the accessibility specialist before sign-off.

## Performance notes
Amend round-trip target <=500 ms p95 is annotated so the pending treatment is designed for a visible but short wait, not an indefinite spinner.

## Observability
Controls annotated with the `position.stop_modified` / `position.tp_ladder_set` audit events they trigger server-side.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All states designed in both themes and densities.
- [ ] CMP-120 spec complete including the translation readout.
- [ ] Keyboard-equivalence mapping reviewed and signed by the accessibility specialist.
- [ ] Every catalogue checklist item ticked with evidence.
- [ ] Contrast verified per frame.

title: Contribute CMP-158, the native-SL affordance pattern and motion to the DS
body:
## Context
`CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice` appears on SCR-060, SCR-062, SCR-064, SCR-065, SCR-066, SCR-067, SCR-068, SCR-069, the trading-defaults settings screen and the per-account profile screen. If each screen styles it locally the product will say the same safety guarantee eight slightly different ways, which is exactly how a guarantee stops reading as a guarantee. `16-design-system-brief.md` requires new patterns to enter the system rather than living as one-offs, and `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 3.1 makes "any new component has a design-system entry, not an ad hoc one-off" a Story DoR item.

E32 is the first epic where the native-SL affordance is designed in anger, so E32 owns publishing it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Publish `CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice` to the design system: anatomy, the single canonical copy pattern, placement rules, the persistent-`role="note"` requirement (never tooltip, never toast), variants (informational guarantee versus active-refusal explanation), light/dark, both densities.
- Publish the **native-SL affordance pattern**: how a non-removable field behaves when cleared (restore + explain), how native versus engine-managed is badged, and where the residual-risk note must appear. Documented as a pattern page with do/don't examples drawn from E32-D03/D04/D05.
- Motion specification for E32's surfaces: modal open/close, the pending -> applied and pending -> rejected transitions, per-child placement progress, and validation-message entry — with durations, easing and the reduced-motion fallback for each, per `16-design-system-brief.md` motion tokens.
- Update `15-component-catalogue.md` entries for CMP-119, CMP-120, CMP-158 and CMP-228 with the finalised specs.
- Storybook design-side documentation for the pattern so engineering implements it once.

## Out of scope
- Implementation of the components (owned by the consuming FE stories and the design-system engineering team), the a11y review (E32-D07), design QA (E32-D08).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The safety notice has one canonical form
  Given CMP-158's ten consuming surfaces
  When the pattern is published
  Then one canonical copy pattern and one placement rule cover all of them, with documented variants rather than per-screen bespoke treatments

Scenario: Motion respects reduced-motion
  Given each specified transition
  Then a prefers-reduced-motion fallback is specified that preserves the state change's legibility without animation, and the pending-to-applied transition remains distinguishable without motion

Scenario: The pattern page carries do/don't examples (edge)
  Given the tooltip anti-pattern that this rule exists to prevent
  Then the page shows the incorrect tooltip treatment as an explicit "don't" alongside the correct persistent note
```

## Technical notes / design
Only existing motion and colour tokens may be used; if a new token is genuinely required it is proposed to the design-system team through their intake, and this ticket records the outcome. The notice's copy is owned jointly with the content owner and must match the message enforced by E32-T01's error path.

## Test plan
N/A — design artefact. Verification: design-system team review and acceptance into the library; Storybook docs page published.

## Security notes
The pattern's wording must state the guarantee accurately — it must not overclaim (e.g. it must not imply protection during an exchange outage) since it is the primary user-facing statement of a safety control. Reviewed with the Security engineer for accuracy of claim.

## Accessibility notes
The pattern mandates `role="note"` for the persistent guarantee and `role="alert"` for active refusals, specifies contrast for both variants in both themes, and forbids conveying the guarantee by colour alone.

## Performance notes
Motion durations kept within the design system's existing budget so modal transitions do not delay interaction readiness.

- [ ] Motion spec published with reduced-motion fallbacks.

title: Build the zero-escape native-SL invariant suite as a required merge check
body:
## Context
R3 exit criterion #2 (`30-release-roadmap.md` section 7.3) is a test, not a feature: *"an automated test suite attempts, by every available path (ticket, chart drag, DOM click, rule action, fan-out, emulated algo), to open a position without a native exchange-side SL — all attempts are rejected, logged, and audited. Zero escapes."* Section 7.4's Safety gate makes this suite a **required check** — a failure blocks merge, not just release. This ticket builds that suite.

The suite must be written so paths that do not exist yet (E31 chart drag, E33 algos, E34 fan-out, E35 rule actions) are enumerated as **expected-present** cases that fail loudly when their epic lands without wiring into the choke point — otherwise the suite silently shrinks to whatever exists today, which is the exact failure mode it is meant to prevent.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `tests/safety/test_native_sl_invariant.py` — a parametrised suite over an explicit `ENTRY_PATHS` registry.
- Registry entries, each with an owning epic: `order_ticket` (E30), `chart_drag` (E31), `dom_click` (E31), `bracket` (E32), `scaled_ladder` (E32), `dca_ladder` (E32), `rule_action` (E35), `fanout_leg` (E34), `emulated_oco` (E33), `emulated_iceberg` (E33), `emulated_twap` (E33), `emulated_chase` (E33).
- Each path is exercised at the **highest layer it owns** (API call for backend paths, Playwright action for UI paths) attempting a position-opening order with no stop; the assertion is threefold: rejected, no request reached the exchange adapter (strict adapter mock that fails the test if called), and an audit row exists.
- A registry completeness test: every path marked `implemented=False` must carry a linked ticket key; when that ticket's epic is merged, CI fails until the flag is flipped and the case passes — so a new entry path cannot be added without registering it.
- An **adapter-level backstop test** independent of the registry: fuzz `PlaceOrderRequest` payloads through `OMS.submit` and assert the property "position-opening implies stopLoss present or pending-attach row exists".
- The single-call-site architecture test from E32-T01 is wired into this suite so the choke point and the escapes are gated together.
- CI wiring as a required check on `main` with no skip/allow-failure, plus a nightly full run against recorded demo fixtures.
- A published "zero escapes" report artefact per run, retained for the R3 PRR evidence pack.

## Out of scope
- The invariant implementation itself (E32-T01/T02); chaos scenarios (E32-Q05); the abuse-case suite from an attacker's perspective (E32-X02, which complements this from outside the trust boundary).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every implemented path is proven to reject
  Given the ENTRY_PATHS registry
  When the suite runs
  Then every path marked implemented attempts a stopless position-opening order, is rejected, reaches no adapter call, writes an audit row, and the run reports zero escapes

Scenario: An unimplemented path is tracked, not forgotten
  Given a path marked implemented false
  Then the suite asserts it carries a linked ticket key and reports it as pending coverage, and the aggregate report states how many paths remain unproven

Scenario: A new entry path that bypasses the choke point fails the build (failure)
  Given a change adding a second call site of adapter.place_order
  When CI runs
  Then the architecture test fails and the merge is blocked

Scenario: The fuzz backstop catches a classification bug (edge)
  Given a mutation that misclassifies a hedge-mode increasing order as reduce-only
  When the property test runs
  Then the property "position-opening implies protected" fails with a minimal reproducing payload

Scenario: The suite cannot be skipped (edge)
  Given a PR marking the safety job as allowed to fail
  Then branch protection rejects the configuration change, because the safety suite is a required check per roadmap section 7.4
```

## Technical notes / design

title: Write the black-box test plan for scaled and DCA ladders
body:
## Context
`US-ALGO-004` and `US-ALGO-009` concentrate their risk in arithmetic and in partial-failure handling — the two things that are hardest to verify by reading code and easiest to verify by black-box execution with awkward numbers. `24-internal-schemas.md` section 10.6 specifies rounding, duplicate-price merging, remainder placement and sub-minimum redistribution precisely enough that each rule is independently testable, and `US-ALGO-009`'s NFR ("projected risk computed for the fully-filled ladder, never for the first leg alone") is a single sentence that, if wrong, lets a trader ladder straight through their risk cap.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Test plan `docs/qa/plans/e32-ladders.md` covering `US-ALGO-004` and `US-ALGO-009`.
- Arithmetic scenarios executed against deliberately awkward instruments and sizes: quantities that do not divide evenly, price ranges narrower than `levels * tickSize` (forcing duplicate-price merges), totals near the minimum notional, 2-level and 50-level boundaries, each distribution (equal, linear, geometric, custom) and skew above and below 1.
- Verification that the preview table and the placed orders match exactly, level by level, in every arithmetic scenario — this is the single highest-value check in the plan.
- Partial-placement scenarios: one leg rejected, several rejected, whole batch rejected, `10018` rate-limit mid-ladder, and per-leg retry behaviour.
- Cancellation scenarios: cancel with none filled, some filled, all filled; verification that a filled portion keeps its protective orders and stays natively stopped.
- DCA scenarios: multiplier laddering, shared-stop behaviour as legs fill, risk-cap refusal with the projected fully-filled figure stated, and the concurrent-leg cap queueing.
- Fixtures named: `batch_partial_success`, `batch_rate_limited`, `batch_full_reject`, `ladder_cap_breach`.
- Traceability table to E32-S03's Gherkin scenarios and to E32-S06's UI scenarios.

## Out of scope
- Bracket/trailing cluster (E32-Q02), automation (E32-Q04), chaos (E32-Q05), perf (E32-Q06), a11y (E32-Q07).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Preview and placement are compared level by level
  Given each arithmetic scenario
  When the ladder is previewed and then placed
  Then every level's price and quantity in the preview matches the corresponding placed order exactly, and any divergence is a P0 finding

Scenario: The fully-filled risk projection is verified against the cap
  Given a DCA ladder whose first leg is within the cap but whose fully-filled position is not
  Then the plan verifies the request is refused before any order is sent and the stated projection equals the fully-filled figure, not the first leg's

Scenario: Sub-minimum redistribution is verified, not assumed (edge)
  Given a ladder whose last two levels round below the instrument minimum
  Then the plan checks which levels were dropped, that their quantity was redistributed proportionally, that the response named them, and that the placed total still equals the requested total

Scenario: A partial batch failure is verified end to end (failure)
  Given a batch where legs 2 and 4 are rejected
  Then the plan verifies the other legs remain working, the failures carry their exchange reasons, retry affects only the failed legs, and the audit record reflects the partial outcome
```

## Technical notes / design
Scenarios pin a specific demo instrument and its `tickSize`/`qtyStep`/`minOrderQty` so expected values are exact numbers in the plan, not formulas the tester must evaluate under time pressure. Where Bybit demo will not reliably produce a partial batch failure, the plan specifies the fixture-driven equivalent and says so.

## Test plan
Dry run once on staging before sign-off; expected values recomputed independently by a second person for the arithmetic scenarios (two independent derivations, because a plan that repeats the implementation's arithmetic mistake proves nothing).

## Security notes
Demo only. The "50-level ladder starves the protective reserve" abuse case is owned by E32-X02; this plan cross-references it rather than duplicating it.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — a11y coverage of SCR-065 is E32-Q07.

## Performance notes
The plan includes a step verifying the preview responds within one frame perceptually and that submission is a single backend request regardless of level count.

## Observability
Steps name the expected `algo.scaled_created` / `algo.scaled_partially_cancelled` audit rows and the `oms_scaled_levels_submitted_total` increments.

title: Automate the Playwright E2E suite for the three E32 screens on demo
body:
## Context
R3's E2E quality gate (`30-release-roadmap.md` section 7.4) requires Playwright coverage on **web and Electron** for ticket, chart trading, DOM trading, **bracket**, fan-out, rules, alerts and journal. E32 owns the bracket, ladder and SL/TP editor share of that gate. `03-testing-strategy.md` places E2E at the top of the pyramid: few, high-value, whole-journey tests — so this suite covers the journeys the unit and integration layers structurally cannot.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Playwright specs under `e2e/specs/e32/`, running against staging (demo) in **both** the web build and the Electron shell.
- Journeys: (1) build and submit a bracket with a stop and single TP via SCR-069, verify the group appears in the blotter and the position is natively stopped; (2) build a 5-level scaled ladder via SCR-065, verify the preview table matches the placed orders, then cancel the group; (3) open SCR-064 on a live demo position, apply a 1.5% trail, verify the translated distance is displayed and the change resolves from pending to applied; (4) configure a 3-step TP ladder and verify the stop resizes when a leg fills; (5) attempt to clear the stop on each of the three screens and verify the restore-and-explain behaviour.
- Failure-path journeys: unsplittable ladder offering its single-target alternative; risk-cap refusal restating the projection; exchange rejection resolving pending to rejected with the reason shown; position closed while SCR-064 is open.
- Deterministic setup/teardown: each spec creates its own position from a known state and flattens it afterwards, so specs can run in any order and a failed spec cannot poison the next.
- Electron parity: the same specs run in the desktop shell, with any divergence recorded as a Bug rather than a skipped test.
- Wired into CI as a nightly job plus a pre-release gate; flake budget and quarantine policy per `03-testing-strategy.md`.

## Out of scope
- Backend-only paths (covered by E32-Q01/Q02/Q03), perf (E32-Q06), a11y audit (E32-Q07), chaos (E32-Q05).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: All five happy journeys pass in web and Electron
  Given the suite runs against staging demo
  Then each journey passes in both the web build and the Electron shell, and any Electron-only failure is filed as a Bug rather than skipped

Scenario: The preview-versus-placement check is a first-class assertion
  Given the scaled ladder journey
  Then the spec reads the preview table from the DOM and asserts each row against the orders returned by GET /api/v1/orders, failing on any divergence

Scenario: Specs are independent and self-cleaning (edge)
  Given the suite runs in a random order with a deliberately failing spec injected
  Then every other spec still passes, and no demo position or working order is left behind after the run

Scenario: A flaky spec is quarantined, not deleted (failure)
  Given a spec failing intermittently above the flake budget
  Then it is quarantined with a linked Bug and an owner, and the quarantine is visible in the suite report rather than silently removed
```

## Technical notes / design
- Selectors use stable `data-testid` attributes agreed with the FE stories, never CSS classes or text that copy changes will break.
- Waits are event-based (WS state, network idle for the specific request) rather than fixed sleeps, because order placement latency on demo is variable.
- Teardown uses the flatten-all API path with a guard that it only ever runs against a demo-tagged account, asserted at spec start — a teardown that could touch live is itself a safety risk.
- Test data: a dedicated demo sub-account per CI runner to avoid cross-run interference.

## Test plan
Self-verifying: the suite is run 10 times consecutively before sign-off to measure flake rate, which must be under the budget in `03-testing-strategy.md`.

## Security notes
Demo credentials are injected from CI secrets, never committed, and the environment guard asserts the target is demo before any order is placed. Screenshots and traces on failure are scrubbed of account identifiers before upload.

## Accessibility notes
Specs navigate by role and accessible name where practical, which incidentally smoke-tests the accessible names; formal a11y coverage remains E32-Q07's.

## Performance notes
Suite wall-clock under 15 minutes so it can gate releases; parallelised per sub-account.

## Observability
Failures upload Playwright traces plus the backend correlation ids for the failed requests, so a failure is diagnosable without re-running.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All journeys automated and green in web and Electron.

title: Build the chaos scenarios for crash seams, failover and disconnects in E32
body:
## Context
R3's chaos gate (`30-release-roadmap.md` section 7.4) names WS kill mid-order, backend restart mid-TWAP and Postgres failover mid-fan-out. E32's equivalents are narrower and more dangerous: the seam **between an entry filling and its stop being attached** is the exact moment where the product's central safety guarantee is at risk, and `24-internal-schemas.md` section 8.8's 2-second deadline and 10-second alert threshold exist precisely to bound it. A chaos suite that kills the process at that seam is the only way to prove the watchdog (E32-T02) does what it claims.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Chaos specs under `tests/chaos/e32/` using the fault-injection harness from `03-testing-strategy.md`.
- Scenarios: (1) kill the process between entry fill and deferred stop attach; (2) kill it between a ladder leg fill and the stop resize; (3) Postgres failover mid-ladder submission; (4) private WS disconnect mid-bracket with fills arriving during the gap; (5) exchange 5xx on `trading-stop` repeated three times, verifying escalation and the E39 lockout request rather than an automatic flatten; (6) clock skew of +30 s applied mid-trail, verifying the trail does not jump; (7) `10018` rate-limit storm during a 50-level ladder while a protective stop must be placed, verifying the protective reserve holds.
- Each scenario asserts a **recovery invariant**, not just absence of crash: the position ends natively stopped, the DB and exchange agree after reconciliation, no duplicate orders exist, and the audit trail explains what happened.
- Measured recovery times recorded against the specified thresholds (<=2 s deferred attach, <=10 s watchdog protection, <=5 s trail resume).
- A chaos report artefact retained for the R3 PRR evidence pack.
- Scenarios run nightly against staging demo plus on demand before each release.

## Out of scope
- Chaos for emulated algos (E33), fan-out unwind (E34) — though this suite's harness is shared with them.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The fill-to-attach seam never leaves a naked position
  Given the process is killed between an entry fill and its stop attach, repeated 20 times
  When the backend restarts each time
  Then in every run the position is natively stopped within 10 seconds, a critical alert was raised, and an audit trail explains the gap

Scenario: Postgres failover mid-ladder reconciles without duplicates
  Given a failover during batch submission of a 20-level ladder
  Then after recovery the number of working orders matches the exchange exactly, no level was submitted twice (verified by deterministic order link ids), and the group state is consistent

Scenario: Repeated trading-stop failures escalate rather than flatten (failure)
  Given three consecutive exchange 5xx responses on the protective write
  Then the system raises a critical alert, requests an account new-entry lockout, and does not automatically flatten the position

Scenario: The protective reserve survives a rate-limit storm (edge)
  Given a 50-level ladder saturating the order-create budget and a simultaneous protective stop placement
  Then the protective placement succeeds by drawing on the reserve, and the ladder throttles instead

Scenario: A scenario that leaves inconsistent state fails loudly (edge)
  Given any run ending with the DB and exchange disagreeing after reconciliation
  Then the scenario fails with a diff of the two states, rather than passing because no exception was raised
```

## Technical notes / design
- Process kills use SIGKILL at a deterministic seam via an injected fault point compiled out of production builds, so the seam is reproducible rather than probabilistic.
- The 20-repetition requirement on scenario 1 exists because a once-passing crash test proves very little about a race.
- Recovery assertions compare against exchange truth (`GET /v5/position/list`, `/v5/order/realtime`), not against our own DB, since our DB is exactly what might be wrong.
- Clock-skew scenario uses a container time offset rather than mutating system time.

## Test plan
This ticket is a test deliverable. Its verification: each scenario is first run against a deliberately broken build (watchdog disabled, reserve removed) and must fail — a chaos test that passes without the control it verifies is not testing anything.

## Security notes
Chaos runs against demo only, with the environment guard asserted at start. The escalation path (lockout, no auto-flatten) is a safety decision verified here; a regression that introduces auto-flatten must fail this suite. The report is part of the RSK-016 evidence chain and is reviewed by the Security engineer.

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
Recovery-time thresholds are the assertions: 2 s deferred attach, 10 s watchdog protection, 5 s trail resume. Measured values are recorded per run so drift is visible over time.

## Observability
Each scenario asserts that the expected alert fired and that `oms_native_sl_missing_total` / `oms_native_sl_fallback_total` moved as expected — verifying that an operator would actually have seen the incident.

title: Build the perf and load scripts proving budget #4 for E32's order paths
body:
## Context
`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` section 5.2 budget #4 requires order submit -> ack p95 <300 ms end-to-end on demo with the **backend-added portion isolated and asserted at <=50 ms p95**, and it is a **hard gate** regardless of environment. R3 exit criterion #11 restates it. E32 adds three new shapes to that path — a bracket with an attached stop, a batched ladder, and a `trading-stop` write — none of which are covered by E29's baseline scripts, and each of which could plausibly blow the backend-added allowance through extra validation, generation or persistence work.

## Scope / Deliverables
- k6 scripts under `perf/k6/e32/`: (1) bracket submission with attached SL; (2) 10-level batched ladder submission; (3) `trading-stop` write via `PUT /positions/{positionId}/tpsl`; (4) protective amend on fill (the 500 ms target).
- Backend-added isolation: each script runs in two modes — against Bybit demo (end-to-end) and against a recorded-fixture mock adapter (backend-only), so the backend's own contribution is measured rather than inferred.
- Micro-benchmarks committed alongside: `NativeSlGuard.evaluate` (<=1 ms p99), `generate_levels` for 50 levels (<=5 ms), `TrailingTranslator` conversion (<=1 ms).
- A sustained profile: continuous bracket + ladder flow at the per-UID order-create budget for 30 minutes, asserting no latency drift, no lost acknowledgements and correct governor back-off.
- Results published to the perf dashboard with a committed baseline, and CI comparison failing on regression beyond the agreed threshold.
- Frontend-side measurement of the SCR-065 preview recompute within one frame, captured via Playwright tracing.

## Out of scope
- Fan-out multi-account budgets (E34 owns the +10 ms/account sub-clause), engine FPS budgets, ingestion soak.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Budget #4 holds for every new order shape
  Given the bracket, ladder and trading-stop scripts run against demo
  Then submit-to-ack p95 is below 300 ms end-to-end for each shape and the isolated backend-added portion is below 50 ms p95, recorded with the run date and build sha

Scenario: The guard and generator stay inside their micro-budgets
  Given the committed micro-benchmarks
  Then NativeSlGuard.evaluate is under 1 ms p99, generate_levels for 50 levels is under 5 ms, and the trailing conversion is under 1 ms, asserted in CI

Scenario: Sustained flow does not drift (edge)
  Given 30 minutes of continuous bracket and ladder submission at the per-UID budget
  Then p95 at minute 30 is within 10% of p95 at minute 1, no acknowledgement is lost, and rate-limit back-off behaves as specified

Scenario: A regression blocks the merge (failure)
  Given a change pushing the backend-added portion above 50 ms p95
  When CI compares against the committed baseline
  Then the perf check fails and the merge is blocked, because budget #4 is a hard gate
```

## Technical notes / design
- End-to-end runs exclude the uncontrolled Bybit RTT component from the backend-added figure by measuring the adapter's own send-to-receive interval separately, per the measurement convention in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`'s network-conditions note.
- The fixture-mock mode removes venue variance entirely, which is what makes the <=50 ms assertion stable enough to gate on.
- Baselines are committed per build and compared with a tolerance band rather than an absolute threshold, to avoid flapping on shared-runner noise; the absolute budget remains the hard ceiling.

## Test plan
This is a test deliverable. Verification: run each script three times and confirm the spread is small enough for the gate to be meaningful; a metric too noisy to gate on is reported and re-scoped rather than gated blindly.

## Security notes
Demo credentials from CI secrets with an environment guard; the sustained profile must not be pointed at live under any configuration. Results contain no account secrets.

## Accessibility notes
N/A, except the frontend preview measurement which supports SCR-065's one-frame requirement.

## Performance notes

Scripts assert that `order_submit_seconds{transport,env}` and `oms_native_sl_attach_seconds` are populated during the run, so the production dashboards are validated by the same exercise.

## Context
`05-accessibility-standard.md` requires WCAG 2.2 AA with axe-core in CI **and** manual screen-reader passes; `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 8 states there is no "internal tool" exemption. R3's a11y gate specifically calls out that the order ticket, DOM ladder and both rule editors must be fully keyboard-operable — E32's three screens carry two equivalent hard requirements of their own: SCR-064's keyboard path equivalent to chart drag-to-modify, and SCR-065's ladder preview as a real table. E32-D07 verified both in design; this ticket verifies them in the built product, where they are frequently lost.

## Scope / Deliverables
- axe-core automated scans across **every enumerated state** of SCR-064, SCR-065 and SCR-069 (not just the default state), wired into CI as a gate for these routes.

- Contrast verification in light and dark at both densities, including non-text elements (focus indicators, table borders, status colours).
- Reduced-motion verification against E32-D06's spec.

## Context
`04-security-program.md` mandates a STRIDE threat model per epic, and `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 2.1 makes it default-on for any epic touching the OMS or the fan-out safety invariant. E32 is the epic that *owns* that invariant, so its threat model is not a formality: it decides where enforcement lives, and that decision is an input to E32-T01 rather than a review of it. This ticket therefore runs **before** the guard is built.

R3's security gate (`30-release-roadmap.md` section 7.4) requires all Critical/High findings closed before the train closes.

## Scope / Deliverables
- STRIDE model published as `docs/security/threat-models/e32-brackets-native-sl.md`.
- Data-flow diagram covering: client -> API -> `OMS.submit` -> `NativeSlGuard` -> exchange adapter -> Bybit; plus the watchdog loop, the `trading-stop` write path, the batch ladder path and the rule-engine entry point.
- Trust boundaries marked explicitly, including the boundary between our backend and Bybit (we control neither the venue's availability nor its acknowledgement semantics).
- Per-element STRIDE enumeration with at least: **Spoofing** — a caller acting for an account it does not own; **Tampering** — payload manipulation to strip or widen a stop, or to submit a preview different from what was priced; **Repudiation** — a stop loosened with no attributable audit row; **Information disclosure** — alerts and diagnostics leaking account identifiers or sizes across RBAC boundaries; **Denial of service** — a 50-level ladder exhausting the per-UID budget so a protective order cannot be placed; **Elevation of privilege** — a viewer-role session mutating protective state, or an internal caller bypassing the choke point.
- A ranked findings table with likelihood, impact, and a required control for each Critical/High.
- The explicit architectural recommendation on enforcement placement (single choke point versus per-call-site) with its rationale, handed to E32-T01.
- Abuse cases derived from the model, handed to E32-X02 as its input list.
- Update to `32-risk-register.md` RSK-016 with the modelled attack paths.

The model must address the specific asymmetry that makes this epic dangerous: a native stop is the only protection that survives our backend dying, so every finding is evaluated against the question "does this leave a position protected only by something we control?"

The DoS findings explicitly consider the rate-budget interaction, so the protective reserve's sizing is a security control as well as a performance one.

title: Implement the abuse-case suite, RBAC scope assertions and SAST rules for E32
body:
## Context
E32-Q01 proves the invariant holds for *legitimate* callers using the product's own paths. This ticket attacks it from outside the trust boundary: crafted API requests, wrong-account references, role escalation, replayed idempotency keys and resource exhaustion. `04-security-program.md` requires abuse cases plus SAST/DAST coverage per epic, and `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 3.2 requires a **manual abuse-case check** for anything touching the safety invariant.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `tests/security/e32/test_abuse_cases.py` implementing every abuse case from E32-X01's list, at minimum:
  1. Submit a position-opening order with `stopLoss` omitted, then with it null, empty string, zero, negative, and NaN-like values.
  2. Submit with a `stopLoss` on the wrong side of the entry (a stop that can never trigger protectively).
  3. Submit with `intent` deliberately mislabelled as `take_profit` or `algo_child` to dodge the position-opening classification.
  4. Submit with `reduceOnly=true` while the account has no position (a stopless opening order in disguise).
  5. Request a deferral with a reason not on the closed allow-list, and with a reason string crafted to match by prefix.
  6. Replay a previously successful `orderLinkId` to try to duplicate an entry without a new stop.
  7. Reference another user's `accountId` / `positionId` on every E32 endpoint (horizontal escalation).
  8. Perform every E32 mutation as a `viewer` role and as a `manager` outside their granted account scope (vertical escalation).
  9. Submit a 50-level ladder repeatedly to exhaust the order-create budget, then attempt a protective stop placement (reserve exhaustion).
  10. Attempt to loosen a stop via `PUT /positions/{positionId}/tpsl` without the explicit-override flag, and with a forged override flag.
- Assertions for each: rejected with the correct error code, **no state change**, and an `audit_log` row recording the attempt — per the RBAC matrix requirement in R3 exit criterion #10.
- Semgrep/Bandit custom rules: flag any new call site of `adapter.place_order` or `adapter.set_trading_stop` outside the sanctioned modules; flag any construction of a `PlaceOrderRequest` outside the OMS submission pipeline.
- ZAP/DAST profile additions for the E32 endpoints, including authorization-bypass and parameter-pollution checks.
- A documented **manual abuse-case check** performed by the Security engineer against staging, with results recorded on the ticket.

## Out of scope
- Penetration testing (E43), key-vault attacks (E27), the functional invariant suite (E32-Q01).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every abuse case is rejected with no state change
  Given each of the ten abuse cases
  When executed against staging demo
  Then each is rejected with the documented error code, a database diff before and after shows no state change, and an audit row records the attempt with the actor

Scenario: Horizontal and vertical escalation are both blocked
  Given a manager scoped to account A and a viewer role
  When either attempts any E32 mutation on account B, or the viewer attempts any mutation at all
  Then the response is 403, no state changes, and an audit row exists for every disallowed combination

Scenario: The reserve survives deliberate exhaustion (failure)
  Given repeated 50-level ladders saturating the order-create budget
  When a protective stop placement is attempted
  Then it succeeds by drawing on the protective reserve, and the attack is visible in metrics

Scenario: A new unsanctioned call site fails SAST (edge)
  Given a change introducing a direct adapter.place_order call outside the OMS pipeline
  When Semgrep runs in CI
  Then the custom rule fires and the build fails with a message naming the sanctioned path
```

## Technical notes / design
- Database diffing uses a transactional snapshot before and after each case; "no state change" is asserted mechanically rather than by inspection.
- Case 5's prefix-matching variant exists because allow-lists implemented with `startswith` are a recurring real-world bypass.
- Case 6 depends on E29's idempotency semantics; the assertion is that the replay is a no-op returning the original result, never a second order.
- The suite runs in CI on every PR touching `services/oms/**` and nightly in full.

## Test plan
This is a security test deliverable. Verification: each case is first run against a deliberately weakened build (allow-list widened, RBAC check removed, reserve disabled) and must fail — proving the case tests the control rather than the happy path.

## Security notes
Runs against demo with the environment guard asserted. Findings are triaged with the Security engineer; any Critical/High must be fixed before the epic closes per R3's security gate. The suite becomes part of the standing regression set cited in E43's pen-test scope.

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
Case 9 deliberately stresses the rate budget; it runs in an isolated window so it does not distort E32-Q06's measurements.

## Observability
Each case asserts the expected audit row and, where applicable, the expected metric increment — so an attack would be visible to an operator, not only blocked.

- [ ] All ten abuse cases implemented and passing, with negative verification against weakened builds.
- [ ] Custom Semgrep/Bandit rules committed and firing in CI.

- [ ] Manual abuse-case check performed and recorded by the Security engineer.

title: Perform the security review and sign-off of the shipped E32 surface
body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 2.2 requires a Security-engineer sign-off comment for any epic labelled `security`, with the STRIDE model finalised and findings triaged; section 8 makes that mandatory for anything touching the fan-out safety invariant. R3's security gate requires all Critical/High closed before the train closes. E32 is the epic whose failure mode is a genuinely unprotected position, so its sign-off is also the primary evidence for RSK-016 in the R3 PRR and the input to E43's pen-test scoping.

## Scope / Deliverables
- White-box review of the shipped code for `NativeSlGuard`, `UnprotectedPositionWatchdog`, `BracketSupervisor`, `ScaledSupervisor` and `TrailingTranslator`, focused on: the completeness of the position-opening classification, the closed deferral allow-list, the ratchet's correctness, transaction ordering (persist before send), and the absence of any bypass path.
- Verification that the two architecture tests (single call site for `place_order` and for `set_trading_stop`) are present, required, and cannot be skipped.
- Review of the E32-X01 findings table: every Critical/High closed with evidence, every accepted risk carrying Owner sign-off and a detection control.
- Confirmation that E32-Q01's zero-escape suite and E32-X02's abuse suite are both required checks with no allow-failure configuration.
- Review of E32-Q05's chaos report specifically for the escalate-not-flatten behaviour and the recovery-time evidence.
- RBAC verification for the E32 routes against the matrix, confirming 403 plus no state change plus an audit row for every disallowed role/route combination.
- Audit-completeness check: every stop modification, ladder creation and refusal produces an attributable, hash-chained audit row.
- SAST/SCA/secrets-scan review across the E32 changes, with findings triaged.
- Published sign-off comment with an explicit residual-risk statement, plus the E32 section of the R3 PRR evidence pack and the pen-test scope note for E43.

## Out of scope
- Fixing defects found (filed as Bugs against the owning tickets), the pen-test itself (E43), live enablement gating (E44).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The invariant has no reachable bypass
  Given the shipped OMS code
  When the reviewer traces every path that can reach the exchange adapter
  Then all of them pass through the guard, the architecture tests enforce it, and the reviewer records the traced paths in the sign-off

Scenario: Every Critical and High finding is closed with evidence
  Given the E32-X01 findings table
  Then each Critical or High is closed with a named test or control as evidence, or is an accepted risk with Owner sign-off and a detection control

Scenario: RBAC holds for every route and role
  Given the E32 routes and the role matrix
  Then every disallowed combination returns 403 with no state change and an audit row, verified by executing the matrix rather than reading the code

Scenario: Sign-off is withheld on an open High (failure)
  Given an open High finding at review time
  Then sign-off is withheld, the epic cannot reach Done, and the blocking finding is stated explicitly on the epic
```

## Technical notes / design
The review is white-box and deliberately adversarial: the reviewer's working question is "how would I open a position without a stop", and the sign-off records the paths tried and closed, so a future reviewer can see what was already considered.

## Test plan
N/A — review. Verification: the RBAC matrix is executed, not inspected; the architecture tests are run against a deliberately violating branch to confirm they fail.

## Security notes
This ticket is the epic's security gate. The sign-off and its residual-risk statement are cited by the R3 PRR (`07-release-and-prr.md`) and by E43's pen-test scoping, and are stored in the restricted security space.

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
The reviewer confirms that the protective reserve's sizing, as shipped, still guarantees a protective token under E32-Q06's measured peak load — a performance number being used as a security control.

## Observability
Confirms that every preventive control also has a detection control where E32-X01 required one, and that alerts route somewhere a human will see them.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] White-box review completed with traced paths recorded.
- [ ] All Critical/High findings closed or accepted with Owner sign-off.
- [ ] RBAC matrix executed for all E32 routes.
- [ ] Architecture tests verified to fail on a violating branch.
- [ ] SAST/SCA/secrets scans clean or triaged.
- [ ] Sign-off comment posted with a residual-risk statement.
- [ ] E32 section of the R3 PRR evidence pack and the E43 pen-test scope note delivered.

`E32-X02` (abuse-case results), `E32-Q05` (chaos evidence), and implicitly all shipped E32 engineering tickets.
